item.title: 'Commanding' star's agents sent to Liverpool to discuss his next steps
item.description: 'Commanding' star's agents sent to Liverpool to discuss his next steps Liverpool have been linked with several different players over the last couple of years. The Anfield outfit have now spent over £600 million on new talent and, while a lot of the players that they chose to bring in have helped improve things, there are still some major problem areas among their ranks. If the Reds are wanting to get back to their best, they're going to need to start spending big or, at least smarty. Because, even though almost £400 million has been spent on their attack , they could still do with adding another forward or two to their squad. But, that area of their squad isn't the only issue that they have. Ifeanyi Ndukwe's agents were sent to Liverpool to discuss his future Much like Liverpool's attack, a decent chunk of change has been spent on trying to improve their defence. And, while things are definitely better with Jeremy Jacquet as Virgil van Dijk's partner rather than Ibrahima Konate , there are still a fair few problems that are affecting Andoni Iraola's men. Neither of their left-backs have performed to the standards expected of them and, while Ronald Araujo has done a good job at right-back , he's not attacking enough to be able to be the Reds' first-choice for the entire season. The fact that so many of the Reds' defenders have their contracts expiring in June 2027 is also a major issue. So, this recent update from Sky Sports Austria journalist Eric Niederseer about what's happening with Ifeanyi Ndukwe makes a lot of sense. "Ifeanyi Ndukwe (18) has already collected the points to qualify for UK work permit after his debut for UD Levante in September," he wrote . "His agents at More Than Sport by AS1 will travel to UK to meet with Liverpool FC and discuss a potential winter return and next career steps." Ifeanyi Ndukwe has the potential to be Liverpool's next Virgil van Dijk Although Ndukwe is only 18 years old, the way that he carries himself on the pitch is impeccable. During Liverpool's pre-season games, fans were distraught that the Austrian couldn't be registered due to his inability to earn a work permit. This led to a fair few rumours about his future being shared with only a season-long loan considered as a potential option by Liverpool. In the end, La Liga outfit Levante took a chance on the youngster and, although it took him a while to get into the swing of things, he's now found his feet and has been one of their best defenders. Obviously, with how well Jacquet and Van Dijk are playing at the moment, it's unclear whether Liverpool really need to bring the Austrian back to L4 in January or not. Because, if he stays put and continues in this purple patch of form, his development could sky-rocket, whereas, if he returns to Liverpool and isn't played each week, he could regress and get worse. item.title: Aston Villa v Manchester City buildup, Premier League news, WSL, and more – matchday live
item.description: ⚽ All the latest as we build up to Saturday’s games ⚽ Ten things to look out for | Fixtures | Mail David Just under three hours to go before Villa Park witnesses people defiantly waving inflatable bananas while being called cheats. Taha Hashim looks at Aston Villa v Man City in the second entry of this week’s, count ‘em, ‘10 Things’. “It was five months ago but it feels a lot longer. When these two sides met in May to finish the season, the contest doubled as Pep Guardiola’s leaving party after 10 years in the job and twice as many trophies, an era now laden with asterisks. It must be surreal for Aston Villa supporters, too. Their 2-1 victory at the Etihad Stadium, inspired by two goals from Ollie Watkins to complete a league double over City, came only four days after their Europa League triumph in Istanbul, where Youri Tielemans, Morgan Rogers and Emi Buendía were the scorers. Buendía is the only one left in claret and blue as Unai Emery builds a new side.” Jamie Jackson’s latest piece listing supposed solutions for MUFC fails to mention the only one that will really work long term. Relegation, preferably “doing a Leicester”, in order to finally get rid of the Glazers. As long as they are there, nothing will meaningfully change. Even if we never got back to being “elite”, at least I might be able to love my club once again. Continue reading...

item.title: Skip Bayless gives unwanted 76ers verdict to Knicks after 0-2 start to season
item.description: Photo by Ian Maddox for The Washington Post via Getty Images Skip Bayless has sent a blunt message to the New York Knicks after their 0-2 start to the NBA season, declaring that the Philadelphia 76ers are already well ahead of their Eastern Conference rivals. The Knicks lost 106-100 to Philadelphia in their season opener before suffering a narrow 107-103 defeat to the Boston Celtics, leaving them searching for their first win. Meanwhile, the 76ers have made a perfect start, winning both games and showing why their new-look roster is attracting so much attention. Skip Bayless backs Philadelphia 76ers over struggling New York Knicks Reacting to New York’s defeat against Boston, Bayless made his feelings clear on X, writing: “Knicks lose at Boston, fall to 0-2. From what I’ve seen so far: SIXERS>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>KNICKS” The post comes after Bayless praised Philadelphia following its remarkable comeback against the Cleveland Cavaliers, when the 76ers overturned a 29-point first-half deficit to win 114-106. The victory came despite a difficult start for LeBron James, who committed five turnovers in the first half of his Philadelphia home debut. Bayless criticised the veteran during the game but acknowledged the team’s quality after the comeback. Speaking in a video posted on X, he said: “All I know is this is the best team in the East. Knicks, you are officially in trouble. Enjoy, LeBron.” Tyrese Maxey led the way against Cleveland with 32 points, while Joel Embiid and Jaylen Brown also made significant contributions. James finished with 17 points and nine rebounds as Philadelphia completed an impressive turnaround. Maxey has averaged 30 points across the 76ers’ opening two games, reinforcing the view that he remains central to the team’s offence despite the arrival of established stars. Philadelphia’s early success has also raised expectations following the additions of James and Brown. The combination of their experience with Maxey’s scoring and Embiid’s presence gives the 76ers plenty of options as they look to establish themselves among the Eastern Conference’s leading contenders. New York, meanwhile, will be keen to respond after two close defeats. Their opening loss to Philadelphia showed the challenge they face against their rivals, while the narrow result against Boston offered little comfort in the standings. There is plenty of basketball left to play, but Bayless has already made his position clear. The Knicks need a win soon, while the 76ers have given their rivals an early reason to pay attention. item.title: Inside Paris' NFL stadium details: Everything to know about Stade de France for Steelers vs. Saints
item.description: Inside Paris' NFL stadium details: Everything to know about Stade de France for Steelers vs. Saints originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The NFL continues its international series this weekend as the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints make history in Paris, France. This will be the first time that the NFL has a game played in France, expanding its reach to another part of the world. Paris is one of the biggest cities in the world, and home to some exciting sports teams, so the NFL is considering this a milestone moment. A game this important needs a stadium that fits the bill, which is what France was able to offer the league. The Saints and Steelers will be playing their game in one of the premier stadiums in Europe, Stade de France, which has hosted so many important events in the last three decades. Here's what you need to know about Stade de France. MORE: SN's latest NFL power rankings for Week 7 Where is Stade de France? Stade de France is located in Saint-Denis, which is a suburb just outside of Paris. As it is a much newer stadium, Stade de France was easier to build on the outskirts of Paris instead of in the heart of the city, which was considered too small to host it. MORE: Potential Troy Aikman landing spots should he leave ESPN Stade de France capacity Stade de France can hold a maximum capacity of 81,338 people, which is right in line with some of the largest capacities among NFL stadiums. When the Saints and Steelers take the field, it shouldn't feel too different than a typical football stadium in the United States. MORE: The Sporting News' latest 2027 NFL Mock Draft When did Stade de France open? Stade de France opened in 1998 , just months before the country hosted the 1998 FIFA World Cup. The entire project and construction occurred because Paris wanted a new stadium to use for hosting the World Cup, something that France hadn't done since 1938. Before Stade de France opened, Parc des Princes, which is the home of Paris Saint-Germain, was the primary sports and event venue in the city. Once Stade de France was built, though, it instantly became one of the biggest and most popular stadiums in Europe. MORE : Who is better: Drake Maye or Caleb Williams? Who plays at Stade de France? Stade de France is considered the national stadium of France, as it is the home stadium for France's national soccer and rugby teams. The stadium has been the backdrop for soccer in France as Les Bleus have grown into one of the best in the world. item.title: Thierry Henry and Kate Scott set to host the upcoming Ballon d’or ceremony
item.description: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 15: Kate Abdo speaks during LIVE On Netflix: Jake Paul vs. Mike Tyson at AT&T Stadium on November 15, 2024 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Brett Carlsen/Getty Images for Netflix © 2024) | Getty Images for Netflix © 2024 The 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony is right around the corner, and the organizers have revealed who will be hosting the gala . Former Arsenal and Barcelona legend Thierry Henry and Briti sh sports broadcaster Kate Scott have been named as the co-hosts for the upco ming 20 26 Ballon d’Or ceremony, which will take place on Monday, October 26, at the London Palladium Theatr e. The ceremony will rev eal the winner of the cov eted prize awarded by France Football in collaboration with UEFA. The duo of Scott and Henry is well-known for their work at CBS Sports, where they have become popular for their UEFA Champions League coverage alongside former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher and former Manchester City defender Micah Richards. Thierry Henry needs no introduction for football fans: with France, he won the 1998 FIFA World Cup in his home country, as well as EURO 2000. On the club side, Henry won two English Premier League titles with Arsenal — one in the 2001/02 season and another in the 2003/04 season as part of The Invincibles , the 2004 Arsenal team that won the league without a single defeat. As if that were not enough, he was a key player for the Barcelona squad that won the 2009 UEFA Champions League, and he was nominated nine times for the Ballon d’Or himself. Scott, meanwhile, has become one of the most recognizable faces in international football broadcasting. A multilingual broadcaster, she often uses her language skills to interview players and coaches or translate for her colleagues. As a journalist, Scott has covered multiple men’s and women’s World Cups, the UEFA Champions League, and several domestic leagues. She is also known for her wit and humor, with colleagues Henry and Richards commonly the targets of her banter. Scott will be a familiar face at the ceremony, having previously hosted in 2014, 2015, and 2025. The ceremony will take place on Monday, October 26, at 8:00 PM GMT at the London Palladium Theatre, where one of the three top candidates — Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane, FC Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal, or Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé — will be crowned as the best footballer in the world. item.title: Gabby Williams reveals if Valkyries walking out of national anthem is a protest
item.description: Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images The Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream have been drawing attention for walking off the court ahead of the national anthem playing during the first three games of this year’s WNBA Finals. The Dream have a 2-1 lead in the series ahead of Game 4, with Angel Reese’s starring displays potentially set to see her be this year’s Finals MVP. But while the basketball has been enthralling, a lot of attention has been put on the players not staying on the court for the national anthem. Dream and Valkyries players have received backlash for their actions, but Gabby Williams has insisted it’s not a protest. Gabby Williams says Golden State Valkyries walking out of national anthem is not a protest In a recent interview, Williams was asked: “Gabby you said protesting is good. Your team isn’t on the court for the national anthem, is that a protest?” She responded: “No,” before being asked: “So why is the team not on the court during the US national anthem before these games.” The Valkyries star responded: “[That’s been] part of our routine for like seven years now.” Game 4 of the Finals kicks off on Saturday at the State Farm Arena. It remains to be seen if the players will stay on the court for the national anthem after not doing so for the opening three. Read more: Caitlin Clark’s contract dilemma awaits Indiana Fever after Amber Cox firing Stephen A. Smith blames Caitlin Clark fans for sleeping on Angel Reese ‘If they continue…’ – Lara Trump warns WNBA over national anthem snub

item.title: 'His bum is a bit big, no?' R Ashwin involved in hilarious exchange on SA captain Temba Bavuma's 'glutes'
item.description: 'His bum is a bit big, no?' R Ashwin involved in hilarious exchange on SA captain Temba Bavuma's 'glutes' originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: R Ashwin and Indian-origin Australian cricket journalist Bharat Sundaresan were involved in a hilarious exchange while discussing South Africa captain Temba Bavuma. The chat happened on Ashwin’s YouTube channel in Tamil. Ashwin poked fun at Sundaresan after he hilariously struggled to describe how Bavuma's strong glutes helped his technique as a batter. R Ashwin and Bharat Sundaresan share hilarious exchange on Temba Bavuma’s glutes' R Ashwin found himself struggling to contain both shock and laughter during a conversation with Australian cricket journalist Bharat Sundaresan about South Africa captain Temba Bavuma. Sundaresan, who was born in India, is ethnically Tamil and frequently converses with Ashwin in Tamil on the former Indian cricketer’s YouTube channel . Their conversations can take a humorous turn, particularly when Sundaresan searches for the right words to express himself. That's because Sundaresan evidently isn't as fluent in Tamil as he is in English. So it's bound to create some hilarious moments like this one. Sundaresan is currently covering the Australian cricket team's tour of South Africa, where the Proteas captain had made a significant contribution in the second Test at Gqeberha, scoring 179 as South Africa recovered from a difficult start to declare at 425/9. MORE: 'The new Little Master!' Dale Steyn crowns South African skipper Temba Bavuma with ultimate moniker after majestic 179 vs Australia in Gqeberha The hosts went on to win by an innings and 31 runs, levelling the three-match series at 1-1. Sundaresan began by praising Bavuma’s preparation, saying the South African captain had spent nearly six to seven hours practising in the nets and working on his technique. However, the conversation took an unexpected turn when he tried to find the right words to describe Bavuma’s physique. "I don't know how to say this but his backside... his bum is a bit big, no? I don't know the right word for it," Sundaresan said. Ashwin intervenes to save the embarrassment Ashwin immediately intervened after initially being taken aback by Sundaresan's wording. "It would sound ugly if you put it this way," he joked before using a more technical way of describing what Sundaresan was attempting to say. "That's why he's quick on the turf. Lightning in his field. He's got a very strong glute," Ashwin added. Sundaresan agreed with the explanation, but the exchange became even funnier when couldn't move on from the remark even as the journalist attempted to return to the subject of Bavuma’s batting technique. MORE: Usman Khawaja book name: Release date, Sandpapergate and what to expect from ex-Australia star's 'explosive' book The journalist agreed that "glutes" was a better way to put it; he continued to explain his point about Bavuma

Dale Steyn crowns South African skipper Temba Bavuma with ultimate moniker after majestic 179 vs Australia in Gqeberha The hosts went on to win by an innings and 31 runs, levelling the three-match series at 1-1. Sundaresan began by praising Bavuma’s preparation, saying the South African captain had spent nearly six to seven hours practising in the nets and working on his technique. However, the conversation took an unexpected turn when he tried to find the right words to describe Bavuma’s physique. "I don't know how to say this but his backside... his bum is a bit big, no? I don't know the right word for it," Sundaresan said. Ashwin intervenes to save the embarrassment Ashwin immediately intervened after initially being taken aback by Sundaresan's wording. "It would sound ugly if you put it this way," he joked before using a more technical way of describing what Sundaresan was attempting to say. "That's why he's quick on the turf. Lightning in his field. He's got a very strong glute," Ashwin added. Sundaresan agreed with the explanation, but the exchange became even funnier when couldn't move on from the remark even as the journalist attempted to return to the subject of Bavuma’s batting technique. MORE: Usman Khawaja book name: Release date, Sandpapergate and what to expect from ex-Australia star's 'explosive' book The journalist agreed that "glutes" was a better way to put it; he continued to explain his point about Bavuma's physique and wide stance. But Ashwin, still amused by the earlier remark, interrupted him. He was not ready to let Sundaresan's original description pass without another joke. "Look, please don't do this to me. The way you said it, 'His backside was big, bum part,' it seems. You've been travelling with the team for so long. Can't you call it glutes?" Ashwin asked, joking of course. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Crikipidea (@crikipidea) Sundaresan then attempted to clarify what he meant, explaining that he was referring to Bavuma’s shape rather than simply naming the muscle. "That's correct. But glutes is still the muscle, I'm talking about the shape. Okay, anyway, leave all that," he responded. The clarification did little to help Sundaresan return to his original point. Who is Bharat Sundaresan? Bharat Sundaresan is an award-winning cricket journalist, commentator and author. He has worked with The Indian Express and is associated with Cricbuzz as its Australian correspondent and senior writer. He has also worked as a commentator and authored "The Dhoni Touch," a book about former India captain MS Dhoni. You can find him on X as beastieboy07 . Sundaresan featured on Ashwin's YouTube channel during the Ashes; now, during the South Africa series and he is expected to be featured more, with the India vs Australia series scheduled for early 2027. Do strong glutes make you run faster? Yes, according to Runner's World's Elizabeth Millard, who wrote : "While having strong leg muscles is important when it comes to sprinting, they’re not the biggest driver for launching off the blocks faster or having a speedier end-of-race kick, a recent study (2020) in the journal Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise suggests. Instead, it’s all about the glutes." The gluteal muscles play an important role in running speed, particularly during acceleration and sprinting. The gluteus maximus helps extend the hip and contributes to generating force as a runner pushes off the ground, while other gluteal muscles help stabilise the hips during movement. MORE: ‘A completely different beast’: Suryakumar Yadav reveals Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma’s influence on his fitness and leadership However, having larger glutes does not automatically make someone faster. Sprinting ability also depends on muscle strength, coordination, running technique, stride frequency, and the contribution of other muscles, including the hamstrings and hip flexors. In this case, Ashwin's remark was that Bavuma's strong glutes aligns with good running biomechanics, although that alone may not explain his speed on the field. item.title: Robert Lewandowski backs Barcelona starlet Lamine Yamal for Ballon d'Or but reveals awe at Bayern Munich star Michael Olise
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain v FC Barcelona - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 - Getty Images Sport Robert Lewandowski has identified the two young talents currently captivating his attention, tipping Barcelona sensation Lamine Yamal for future individual honours. However, the legendary striker admitted he is equally mesmerised by the rapid rise of Bayern Munich’s star, Michael Olise. Lewandowski tips Yamal for future glory Former Barcelona striker Lewandowski has little doubt about the ceiling of Yamal . The 19-year-old has taken the football world by storm since his breakthrough, becoming a pivotal figure for both club and country. The Polish forward believes the winger has everything required to eventually be crowned the best player on the planet. Speaking about the youngster's potential, Lewandowski expressed his belief that the La Masia graduate is destined for the highest individual accolade in the game. "Of course, I push my finger for Lamine to win the Ballon d’Or , because he’s amazing, especially for his age, but still, if you compare now to the previous time, it’s a little bit different," said Lewandowski in his interview with The Athletic . Ballon d'Or race blown wide open Setting aside any lingering focus on his own past Ballon d’Or history, Lewandowski candidly reflected on how the landscape for football’s most prestigious individual prize has shifted. He admitted to missing the defining era marked by the fierce back-and-forth between Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, when the race was virtually guaranteed to come down to just two or three overwhelming favorites battling at the pinnacle of the sport. By contrast, Lewandowski noted that the competition has become significantly more open and unpredictable. Rather than being dominated by an exclusive duopoly, today's field presents a wide array of legitimate contenders. "Now, what I see is that it is a little bit more open. Now maybe you can find even 10 players, and you can find arguments why this kind of player is gonna win this Ballon d’Or," he said. Stunned by Michael Olise's impact However, while the hype surrounding Yamal is substantial, Lewandowski is also keeping a keen eye on the Bundesliga. The veteran striker admitted he has been blown away by the performances of Olise at the Allianz Arena. Lewandowski, who is currently playing in Major League Soccer, did not hide his admiration for the former Crystal Palace man. "Olise for me is like: ‘Wow.’ He’s the game-changer player. And I think this work and cooperation between [Harry] Kane, Olise and [Luis] Díaz is like a perfect match," the Pole explained. "But I am impressed that Olise is this kind of player. He has a huge future. I know that everyone is talking about Lamine, but I try to find sometimes the different players and see something, sometimes that not everyone sees yet. For me also, probably if (Olise) scored one or two goals in the World Cup, he would be the favorite also to win the Ballon d’Or, with Lamine or wit

Lewandowski pointed to the Frenchman's maturity as his defining trait. "His decisions are perfect. He masters the timing, he knows when to shoot to score, when to make the pass and what type of pass to perform. I love watching Lamine, but also Olise," he added.

item.title: ‘Skip my graduation’: Ringer host reveals how fate ruined his planned LeBron James hatewatch in 2008
item.description: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images One of The Ringer’s hosts has revealed how much he disliked LeBron James during the prime of his career. LeBron James has started the new chapter of his NBA career with the Philadelphia 76ers on a perfect note as they are 2-0 to start the season. At 41 years old, James may no longer be in the prime of his career, but he’s still playing an important role for the 76ers. As a result, this has James haters in shambles, including The Ringer’s Raheem Palmer. Speaking of whom, Palmer recently shared a story of how much he dislikes the King. Raheem Palmer skipped his graduation to watch LeBron James lose during the 2008 playoffs The Cleveland Cavaliers faced off against the Boston Celtics during the 2008 Eastern Conference Semifinals. The series went to seven games, with the C’s edging out James and the Cavs. Palmer recently recalled the series in light of James’ departure from the Los Angeles Lakers. “I hated LeBron James back in 2008 so much I wanted to skip my graduation from Wharton to stay home, eat wings and watch him lose to the Celtics in Game 7 of the 2008 Eastern Conference Semi-finals. “As fate would have it, my body would not let me wake up. I slept through graduation and my whole family and my ex-girlfriend were p_____ at me,” Palmer wrote on X . The Ringer host then explained now he can happily support the Lakers, but James joining the 76ers is still a bittersweet moment for him. “Anyways, I’m happy to be able to root for the Lakers again without him on my team. I just hate that he’s on my other team [Sixers]. Luka is so much fun,” Palmer added. For what it’s worth, both the Lakers and the 76ers are off to a perfect start to the regular season. James parting ways with the Purple and Gold seems to have done wonders for both sides. Instead of enjoying one side, however, fans like Palmer continue to spew hate towards the 4x NBA champion. Read more: ‘Anybody watch him?’: What LeBron James once said about Dalton Knecht suggests Lakers have messed up Stephen A. Smith says LeBron James ‘deserves better’ after Trump criticism Jason Kidd makes it clear who the number one option on the Philadelphia 76ers’ starting lineup is

item.title: Prosecutors decline filing Oregon’s Evan Stewart’s DUII charge ahead of Illinois clash
item.description: © Ben Lonergan/The Register-Guard / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images. Prosecutors decline filing Oregon’s Evan Stewart’s DUII charge ahead of Illinois clash appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Oregon football is set to face Illinois in a Big Ten matchup without Evan Stewart . Meanwhile, the Oregon Ducks wide receiver’s legal situation has taken an unexpected turn ahead of the team’s upcoming game. Reportedly, prosecutors have declined to file a Driving Under the Influence of Intoxicants (DUII) charge against Stewart. “Prosecutors have declined to file a Driving Under the Influence of Intoxicants charge against Oregon Ducks star wide receiver Evan Stewart following his arrest in Springfield last weekend,” according to KATU News. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Stewart was arrested on suspicion of driving under the influence of intoxicants in Springfield following the Ducks’ game against Nebraska. He was booked into Springfield Municipal Jail at approximately 7 a.m. and released to a third party about an hour later, according to reports citing police information. However, OregonLive reporter Ryan Clarke offered a different explanation after speaking with the Springfield Police Department. According to Clarke, prosecutors were still waiting to receive evidence before determining how to proceed with the case. “Based on my conversation with Springfield PD yesterday, this is inaccurate,” Clarke reported. “Prosecutors are awaiting delivery of evidence, which can sometimes take days or weeks depending on if it was a blood draw, before formally filing charges. That’s why it says “no complaint filed” online.” Stewart’s legal situation comes amid an injury issue that has already affected his availability. The wide receiver missed Oregon’s 17-14 win over Nebraska. Before his absence, Stewart had established himself as one of Oregon’s leading offensive contributors. Through five games, he recorded 27 receptions for 352 yards and four touchdowns. Now, Oregon are set to enter the Illinois game with a 4-2 overall record and a 2-1 mark in Big Ten play. The game is another opportunity for the team to build momentum, but Stewart’s continued absence leaves the team without one of its most productive receivers. Related: Texas’ AD refuses to hit panic button amid Arch Manning slump Related: Kansas State QB Avery Johnson gets doubtful designation vs. Arizona State

Coming off back-to-back title fight victories over Diego Lopes , Volkanovski is riding high on confidence. That’s because nearing age of 40, “The Great” is showing the combat world that he is still fighting at the highest level. Since 2019, all of Volkanovski’s fights (11) have been for some sort of title, whether it be at Featherweight or Lightweight, making him one of the most experienced championship fighters in the sport. How many more years he intends to keep going remains to be seen ( sorta? ), but as long as he keeps winning, I don’t see any reason for him to start winding it down. A loss, however, changes everything . And another title fight may not be in his immediate future, which is something he is not accustomed to. That said, his next challenge is more than capable of dethroning him once and for all … and maybe even send him into retirement . Speaking of which, Evloev is finally getting a long-awaited (and long overdue) title shot. Undefeated (20-0), Evloev is perfect (10-0) under UFC’s banner, defeating the likes of the aforementioned Lopes (who has already had two title fights), Arnold Allen , Aljamain Sterling and more recently, Lerone Murphy . Of course, Volkanovski will be his biggest test to date, but he is more than ready to prove he is indeed the best 145-pound fighter in the game. The only knock on the Russian-born grappler is that he has yet to secure a finish during his run with the promotion, winning all of his bouts by way of decision. That said, a win is a win is a win, and that’s all he knows how to do. That’s not to say that an impressive finish over Volkanovski — who has only been stopped twice in his UFC career — would silence the naysayers and add another threat level to his game. Still, getting the win by any means necessary is the priority here. And Evloev, 32, is ready to upset the order at 145 pounds. Original Card Vs. Actual Card /Injuries A Featherweight bout between Arnold Allen vs. Aaron Pico was scheduled for the event before Allen was forced to withdraw as a result of an injury . He was ultimately replaced by Losene Keita , who is just 1-1 under UFC’s banner and is coming off a big win over Muhammad Naimov , knocking him out in the first round . As for Pico, after getting knocked out in his UFC debut by Lerone Murphy, he bounced back to defeat his former Bellator MMA stablemate, Patricio Pitbull , in his sophomore effort. A win over Keita would get his rhythm going and could be a catalyst to start making a run toward a top ranking spot. New Blood: Asaf Chopurov will make his UFC debut after racking up an undefeated record (11-0) in the minor leagues, with his longest stint being with UAE Warriors. He has five knockouts, five submissions and one decision on his record — he is as well-rounded as they come. His first challenge will come against Colby Thicknesse , who is on a two-fight win streak after stumbling out of the gates with a loss in his Octagon debut. How The ‘Prelims’ Look: Dominick Reyes seems to have been able to turn back the hands of time, winning four of his last five UFC bouts, with his lone defeat coming at the hands of current 205-pound champion, Carlos Ulberg . He is coming off a big win over Johnny Walker , but he will look for an even more convincing win over Azamat Murzakanov , who suffered the first (and only) loss of his UFC career in his most recent fight against Paulo Costa . Abdul-Rakhman Yakhyaev is on his way to making a Light Heavyweight name for himself inside the Octagon, securing three first round stoppage wins under UFC’s umbrella. Meanwhile, his opponent, Nikita Krylov , is headed in the opposite direction, losing three of his last four contests. In fact, this will be his first fight since getting his jaw jacked by Robert Whittaker earlier this year. After a rocky start to his UFC career, Abus Magomedov has gone 4-1 in his last five fights, with his lone loss during that span coming against top-ranked contender, Joe Pyfer . Magomedov has proven to be a formidable foe. That said, he has a huge challenge ahead of him in the form of Cam Rowston , who is on an eight-fight win streak. During his run, he has gone 3-0 with two knockouts inside the Octagon. Nurullo Aliev holds a perfect mixed martial arts (MMA) record (12-0), boasting four straight decision wins inside the Octagon. He wants to keep the momentum going, and he will have a decent challenge in the form of Grant Dawson , who is coming off a submission win over Mateusz Rebecki . “KGD” is 4-1 in his last five fights, but if he can hand Aliev his first-ever loss, his stock would get a huge boost. For the first time in his UFC career, Jacob Malkoun is on a three-fight win streak, and now he will attempt to go for his fourth straight when he battles Abubakar Vagaev (winner of four straight). In his UFC debut, Vagaev defeated Saygid Izagakhmaev via unanimous decision. Noah Gugnon kicked off his UFC career with a bang, defeating Milos Janicic via first round submission just two months ago. He is now back to keep his momentum going in a quick turnaround in an attempt to secure his seventh straight finish when he battles Kody Steele, who is coming off a submission win of his own over Dom Mar Fan . Nicolle Caliari came in nearly five pounds overweight for her Strawweight bout against Iasmin Lucindo , which will cost her a whopping 30 percent cut of her fight purse. It’s not a good look for a fighter who is just 1-2 under UFC’s banner. A loss for her could get her cut by the promotion since she would be 1-3 and her massive scale fail. Who Needs A Win Badly: Bolaji Oki is currently on a two-fight losing streak and has lost three of his last four —all by way of stoppage. He is set to face off against Daniel Santos in a must-win fight. Oki hasn’t gotten off to the start he would have hoped after making his way in via Contender Series , and a third straight loss against Santos — who is coming off a loss himself to Doo Ho Choi — could be his one-way ticket out of the promotion. Interest Level: 8.5/10 Petr Yan vs. Merab Dvalishvili will face off for the third ( and likely final ) time in the co-headlining act in what will be Yan’s first title defense since winning the belt off, you guessed it, Dvalishvili, 10 months ago. “No Mercy” won that fight rather convincingly; however, in their first encounter three years ago, it was Merab who was the superior grappler and striker. Now, one man will look to prevail and put the rivalry in the rear-view mirror once and for all. And barring a draw, that is exactly what should happen. Yan has the better striking , that is no mystery, but when it comes to grappling and controlling the fight

item.title: Lens predicted XI v Paris FC: Ismaelo Ganiou out, Odsonne Édouard dropped?
item.description: Lens predicted XI v Paris FC: Ismaelo Ganiou out, Odsonne Édouard dropped? Whilst not injured, Odsonne Édouard may be left out of RC Lens’ squad to face Paris FC on Sunday night, as per L’Équipe. There is cover for the former Crystal Palace forward. It is Benfica loanee Franjo Ivanovic who is set to lead the line at the Stade Bollaert tonight. There aren’t too many options in this sector for Yannick Cahuzac, however, with Abdallah Sima out injured until after the international break. Lens are missing players at the back, too. Ismaelo Ganiou underwent minor knee surgery this week and is set for a period on the sidelines; Maik Nawrocki is out potentially until the end of the season with an ACL; whilst this game may come too soon for Jonathan Gradit, who is returning from a minor injury. Lens likely line-up v Paris FC Robin Risser; Kyllian Antonio, Samson Baidoo, Ruben Aguilar; Matthieu Udol, Amadou Haidara, Michael Cuissance, Saud Abdelhamid; Florian Sotoca, Franjo Ivanovic, Florian Thauvin. (L’Éq) GFFN | Luke Entwistle
item.content:encoded: Lens predicted XI v Paris FC: Ismaelo Ganiou out, Odsonne Édouard dropped? Whilst not injured, Odsonne Édouard may be left out of RC Lens’ squad to face Paris FC on Sunday night, as per L’Équipe. There is cover for the former Crystal Palace forward. It is Benfica loanee Franjo Ivanovic who is set to lead the line at the Stade Bollaert tonight. There aren’t too many options in this sector for Yannick Cahuzac, however, with Abdallah Sima out injured until after the international break. Lens are missing players at the back, too. Ismaelo Ganiou underwent minor knee surgery this week and is set for a period on the sidelines; Maik Nawrocki is out potentially until the end of the season with an ACL; whilst this game may come too soon for Jonathan Gradit, who is returning from a minor injury. Lens likely line-up v Paris FC Robin Risser; Kyllian Antonio, Samson Baidoo, Ruben Aguilar; Matthieu Udol, Amadou Haidara, Michael Cuissance, Saud Abdelhamid; Florian Sotoca, Franjo Ivanovic, Florian Thauvin. item.content:encoded: VAR Review – Collum admits Celtic should have been awarded a penalty Willie Collum has admitted on his VAR Review show that Celtic should have had penalty at Fir Park and has also confirmed that St Mirren were wrongly denied a spot kick at Ibrox… 18th January 2026; Rugby Park, Kilmarnock, East Ayrshire, Scotland: Scottish Cup Football, Auchinleck Talbot versus Celtic; SFA Referees Chief Willie Collum. Photo Vagelis Georgariou Referee chief Willie Collum has admitted that Celtic were wrongly denied a spot kick in the 2-0 win over Motherwell at Fir park a fortnight ago. The incident in question was a second half goal bound Callum McGregor shot was blocked by the hand of Lukas Fadinger, but despite a VAR check no offence was found to have been committed. 11th October 2026; Fir Park, Motherwell, Scottish Premiership Motherwell versus Celtic; Referee Steven McLean. Photo by Vagelis Georgariou Referee Steven McLean allowed play to continue, with Celtic receiving only a corner. VAR Don Robertson did not intervene to recommend an on-field review. Refereeing pundits all agreed in the aftermath that Celtic should have been awarded at spot kick at Fir Park. 21st May 2026; Firhill Scottish Championship. Partick Thistle versus St Mirren; Referee Don Robertson. Photo Vagelis Georgariou Yet match referee Steven McLean allowed play to continue, with Celtic receiving only a corner. VAR Don Robertson did not intervene to recommend an on-field review. Perhaps the commotion about Celtic getting a correctly awarded penalty at Fir Park on our previous visit to Fir Park had a bearing on the match official’s reluctance to award Celtic a penalty this time around? He told Sky Sports’ VAR Review Show : “Again, I’ve got great sympathy for the Motherwell player because I think he is trying to avoid the contact. As the shot comes in, he’s turning his body away, he’s bringing his leg up to block the ball. “There’s definitely discussion between the referee and the VAR about the arm tucked in. I think the elbow’s tucked in, but the Motherwell player takes a real risk by his arm out from the body here. “And in our opinion, after reviewing this incident, our coaching going forward is that this should be a penalty kick, should be awarded in this incident.” Collum also pointed out that the proximity of the shot was not close enough to exonerate Fadinger. The Head of Referees added: “I don’t think it’s very, very close.” Collum also admit that officials got it wrong by denying St Mirren a penalty in their 1-0 defeat at Ibrox. Ismeal Kabia went down after Manny Fernandez appeared to catch him on the top of the foot. “It should have been a longer check, without a doubt. For us, this is a penalty kick, without question.” A brief VAR check produced the verdict that the winger had “run into” the Rangers defender and no review was recommended. Collum first of all accepted that the check should have been more thorough before admitting that the wrong decision was reached. He added: “It should have been a longer check, without a doubt. For us, this is a penalty kick, without question. “There will be occasions where attackers in the area and there will be inevitable light contact. Here it’s quite clear that this is a reckless contact. “It falls into the category of reckless so a yellow card would be expected here for that kind of stepping action on to the foot. So it’s simple to say the decision is wrong. We would agree with that.” Callum McGregor of Celtic during the Scottish Premiership match between Motherwell and Celtic at Fir Park on October 11, 2026 in Motherwell, Scotland. (Photo by Zak Mauger/Getty Images) So Celtic wrongly denied a penalty in a match we won anyway and the Rangers benefiting from a stonewall penalty being awarded against them in a match they won by a single goal. That is a potential two points swing in their favour. Let’s start keeping the score on this throughout the rest of the season and for fairness assume that every penalty wrongly denied is scored. So as things stand the table is as follows: The Rangers – One incorrect decision UP and TWO points better off Celtic – One incorrect decision DOWN but no points impact Here’s the latest VAR Review… HAVE YOUR SAY – Join the Celtic conversation in our comments section below… Celtic in the Fifties by Matt Corr, in two volumes, both published on 4th September 2026 by Celtic Star Books. item.title: 'He’s a very intelligent player' - Former La Masia coach Pau Moral backs Barcelona youngster Xavi Espart to handle Real Madrid's Yan Diomande in El Clasico
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-PSG-BARCELONA - AFP Former Barcelona youth coach Pau Moral believes breakout defender Xavi Espart possesses the tactical awareness required to keep Real Madrid winger Yan Diomande quiet in Sunday's La Liga clash. The versatile youngster enters the first El Clasico of the campaign in fine form after netting his maiden Champions League goal against PSG in midweek. Academy mentor trusts versatile defender Moral has tipped his former academy charge to excel against Los Blancos' teenage attacker at Spotify Camp Nou on Sunday, October 25. Having impressed at both left-back and right-back this season, Espart is set to retain his starting berth on the right flank while Joao Cancelo covers the opposite side. However, his ex-mentor cautioned supporters not to expect perfection from the developing prospect. Injury crisis forces defensive reshuffle Hansi Flick's reigning champions are turning to the youngster because Jules Kounde is a major doubt with an ankle sprain, while Eric Garcia, Andreas Christensen, Roony Bardghji and Dani Olmo - ruled out for a month after suffering an adductor injury in Paris - are all sidelined. Opposite number Jose Mourinho is also missing suspended talisman Vinicius Junior alongside injured duo Rodrygo and Raul Asencio, meaning Diomande should start on the wing while Federico Valverde deputises at right-back and Bernardo Silva moves inside. Speaking to Cadena SER ahead of the game, Moral backed Espart to cope with the challenge: "I don't think he'll have any trouble defending against Diomande; he's a very intelligent player. We also have to be prepared for him to make mistakes someday. It's not normal for these La Masia lads to never make a single error." Relentless graft fuels senior breakthrough Reflecting on the youngster's rise through the youth ranks alongside fellow graduate Pau Cubarsi, Moral added: "He's a kid who's had to work incredibly hard; he was a dark horse. He wasn't like Gavi or Lamine Yamal, who were practically stars from a young age, but he's worked extremely hard for it. "He personally influenced me as a coach. Sometimes we've had very good players, but without a connection. On the other hand, with players like Cubarsi or Espart, you feel very proud. The goal of everyone at La Masia is precisely for the youngsters to reach the first team. "He's always defended well, even though he was short at La Masia, he already did very well. Now he plays exactly the same as he did six or seven years ago, but against players of a higher calibre. "I'm sold. Espart has great stats, and although he plays very well at full-back, he's really most comfortable in midfield." Title race hinges on Sunday Barcelona welcome their arch-rivals to Catalonia sitting top of the table after winning all nine of their opening league fixtures in the 2026-27 campaign. Victory on Sunday would move Flick's side nine points clear of third-placed Madrid, who currently trail the leaders by six points in Mourinho's second spell in charge.

item.title: Brazil v Norway: first-ever clash for top spot in U17 World Cup Group C
item.description: Brazil v Norway: first-ever clash for top spot in U17 World Cup Group C Brazil and Norway face off this Saturday (24) at 12 p.m. (Brasília time) in the third and final round of Group C at the U-17 Women’s World Cup, at the Mohammed VI Football Complex in Salé, Morocco. This will be their first meeting at a World Cup in this age category, as the teams have never faced each other in previous editions of the tournament. The match wraps up both teams’ group-stage campaigns and will be decisive in determining the group’s final standings. The meeting comes during Norway’s second appearance at a U-17 Women’s World Cup. The European side made its debut in the 2025 edition, while Brazil has competed in the tournament since 2008 and arrives in Morocco for its tenth appearance. Despite Brazil’s longer history, the two teams had never crossed paths in previous editions of the competition. Brazil’s U-17 national team completed preparations last Friday (23) to face Norway in Group C of the U-17 World Cup Credit: Fabio Souza / CBF Brazil aims to repeat historic run The 2026 South American champions in this age category, Brazil is aiming to improve on its performance at the last U-17 World Cup, when it finished fourth, its best-ever result in the tournament. Rilany Silva’s side enters the decisive round with four points, following a resounding 6–2 opening win over Canada and a 3–3 draw with Ghana. Against Canada, Brazil showed attacking strength and clinical finishing to build a commanding lead. Against Ghana, however, despite scoring three goals and taking the lead during the match, Brazil conceded an equalizer in the closing minutes. Nicolly Manuel, Kaillany Ranifah and Indy scored Brazil’s goals in its second match. The result kept the team top of Group C, with nine goals scored and five conceded, but left first place to be decided in the final round. Nicolly Manuel opened the scoring against Ghana in the second round of the U-17 World Cup group stage Credit: Fabio Souza/CBF For the clash with Norway, the coaching staff worked on tactics, positioning and individual responsibilities. Midfielder Carol Melo emphasized the need for greater concentration and attention to detail in the match. “They’re a good opponent. They defend as a unit, play direct football and like a physical battle too. So we’re ready for that,” the player said when assessing Norway’s style. A win would secure top spot in the group for Brazil with seven points. A draw would take the team to five points, while a defeat would allow Norway to overtake Brazil in the standings. Norway seeks first-ever knockout-stage berth Norway enters the final round with three points and a chance to achieve a historic first: reaching the knockout stage of the U-17 Women’s World Cup. In its opening match, the European side beat Ghana 3–0 with a performance that demonstrated its organization and ability to capitalize on chances. item.title: Leclerc tops both Austin practices but warns Verstappen and Antonelli have more in hand
item.description: Charles Leclerc was fastest in both Friday practice sessions at the United States Grand Prix , but he does not think he goes into qualifying as the favourite. The Ferrari driver believes Max Verstappen and Kimi Antonelli have more pace to come, and he says his team's Austin upgrade is smaller than people expected. Leclerc says the upgrade is a small step Once the cars were back in the garage, though, the man at the top of the timesheets was much more cautious at the Circuit of the Americas . Leclerc described the update as a modest package that helped Ferrari start the weekend well, not a big leap forward. "The feeling is quite good, but we need to be careful. Obviously, it's only Friday, and we are seeing what we expected. But, again, it's definitely not what everybody thinks in terms of of upgrade and lap time gains" He also pointed to the pattern he expects from Friday to Saturday. "I think the balance of the car was good, and straight away, we started in a in a good window, and that paid off. And and obviously, all the hard work that has been done in order to bring this upgrade as soon as possible is also helping us a little bit, but we shouldn't carry too high expectations going into tomorrow because I felt like the others have more potential to unlock for sure." Leclerc driving the SF-26 at COTA - Photo: Race Pictures Leclerc driving the SF-26 at COTA - Photo: Race Pictures Leclerc named his rivals: "I mean, Kimi and Max seem to be very, very strong. The McLaren, I don't really know yet. I don't think they put everything together yet, but Kimi and Max will definitely be up there." Hamilton had already lowered expectations Leclerc's caution matches what his teammate said before a lap had been run. At Thursday's press conference, Lewis Hamilton put a figure on the new floor. "We have a very, very small upgrade this weekend. It's less than a tenth. It's like half a tenth," he said, according to The Race. Team principal Fred Vasseur was just as careful on Friday evening. "I'm not sure that the classification of FP1 was always relevant for Qualifying," he told Formula1.com, adding that the impact of the upgrades was "a bit less than at the beginning of the season". Verstappen's deleted lap and the gaps tell a similar story In FP1, Verstappen briefly went faster than Leclerc with a 1:35.8, but the lap was deleted for track limits at Turn 19. Leclerc set a 1:36.0. In the end, the Ferrari driver finished ahead of the four-time world champion by 0.084s. In the second session, Antonelli finished just 0.042s behind, while Verstappen was two tenths of a second off the Monegasque driver's pace.
item.content:encoded: Charles Leclerc was fastest in both Friday practice sessions at the United States Grand Prix , but he does not think he goes into qualifying as the favourite. The Ferrari driver believes Max Verstappen and Kimi Antonelli have more pace to come, and he says his team's Austin upgrade is smaller than people expected. Leclerc says the upgrade is a small step Once the cars were back in the garage, though, the man at the top of the timesheets was much more cautious at the Circuit of the Americas . Leclerc described the update as a modest package that helped Ferrari start the weekend well, not a big leap forward. "The feeling is quite good, but we need to be careful. Obviously, it's only Friday, and we are seeing what we expected. But, again, it's definitely not what everybody thinks in terms of of upgrade and lap time gains" He also pointed to the pattern he expects from Friday to Saturday. "I think the balance of the car was good, and straight away, we started in a in a good window, and that paid off. item.description: Harmony Sample (7), Destiny Ndam-Simpson (18), Gigi Whann (5), Kristen Dear (8) — TUCSON, ARIZ. -- Volleyball vs. Iowa State University at McKale Center at ALKEME Arena. Oct. 2, 2026. | Photo by Ethan Tees / Arizona Athletics Arizona volleyball head coach Rita Stubbs has said repeatedly that there’s no team in the conference that the Wildcats are good enough to look past. That was obvious at West Virginia. The Mountaineers have won a total of five Big 12 matches combined over the last two seasons. Their 3-1 (23-25, 25-15, 25-21, 25-17) win against Arizona on Friday night gave them their fourth conference win of 2026. One constant for Arizona this year has been inconsistencies. The wildly different scores from one set to another backed that up once again. The reason for that was another common story for the Wildcats. “Passing broke down,” Stubbs said. The issue affected even some of Arizona’s stronger passers. Junior outside hitter Carlie Cisneros received 33 serves, far outpacing everyone else on the team. The Mountaineers put a lot of pressure on her. It got to her. “Carlie got aced six times,” Stubbs said. Despite the difficulty in one of the stronger parts of her game, Cisneros contributed her fifth double-double of the season with 10 kills and 11 digs. She also had a block assist and two aces. Her 12.5 points were second on the team. Destiny Ndam-Simpson led the team with 15 kills on .268 hitting. She also had a double-double with 12 digs. Her two aces gave her a team-high 17 points. item.content:encoded: Harmony Sample (7), Destiny Ndam-Simpson (18), Gigi Whann (5), Kristen Dear (8) — TUCSON, ARIZ. -- Volleyball vs. Iowa State University at McKale Center at ALKEME Arena. Oct. 2, 2026. | Photo by Ethan Tees / Arizona Athletics Arizona volleyball head coach Rita Stubbs has said repeatedly that there’s no team in the conference that the Wildcats are good enough to look past. That was obvious at West Virginia. The Mountaineers have won a total of five Big 12 matches combined over the last two seasons. Their 3-1 (23-25, 25-15, 25-21, 25-17) win against Arizona on Friday night gave them their fourth conference win of 2026. One constant for Arizona this year has been inconsistencies. The wildly different scores from one set to another backed that up once again. The reason for that was another common story for the Wildcats. “Passing broke down,” Stubbs said. The issue affected even some of Arizona’s stronger passers. Junior outside hitter Carlie Cisneros received 33 serves, far outpacing everyone else on the team. The Mountaineers put a lot of pressure on her. It got to her. “Carlie got aced six times,” Stubbs said. Despite the difficulty in one of the stronger parts of her game, Cisneros contributed her fifth double-double of the season with 10 kills and 11 digs. She also had a block assist and two aces. Her 12.5 points were second on the team. Destiny Ndam-Simpson led the team with 15 kills on .268 hitting. She also had a double-double with 12 digs. Her two aces gave her a team-high 17 points. In a rare occurrence for this year’s Wildcats, they got all three pin positions into double digits in scoring. Right side hitter Kennedy Osunsanmi had 10 kills on .333 hitting. She added a block assist for 10.5 points. “We had three players with double-digit kills,” Stubbs said. “We competed.” The Wildcats were fairly efficient on offense despite their difficulty with serve receive. Six of the seven players who got a kill hit .250 or better. All three of Arizona’s middle blockers hit .400 or better. That has not always been the case this season as the middles have often struggled with efficiency at a position that should be highly efficient. Journey Tucker had a strong offensive night after several difficult matches in recent weeks. The senior hit .400, her highest hitting percentage since Oct. 2 when she hit .500 against Iowa State. She has hit below .275 in the other five matches this month. Tucker’s frustrations were something Stubbs talked about before the team left for the trip to West Virginia. “If you just get the ball to her at the right tempo, she’s savvy enough and she understands enough what to do with it,” Stubbs said. “But when the ball is low, I mean that’s difficult for anyone, especially when you want to score it, you know what I mean? Or if the ball is slow, that’s when her not-so-good arm swing comes to play…so it gets to be frustrating for her because she knows that it’s not just the setting, and she’ll say it in a heartbeat. She knows that she plays a role in it, as well.” Tucker responded well with seven kills on 15 swings and just one error. What was not as successful for the Wildcats was the block. Arizona has scored a considerable portion of its points this year on its blocking, especially by Tucker. The team ranks in the bottom three in the Big 12 in far too many stats. They are last in six of the 13 statistical categories the conference keeps for teams. They climb out of the basement in digs, blocks, opponent blocks, and opponent aces. The Wildcats average 2.18 blocks per set as a team. They had just three total blocks in the four-set match against the Mountaineers. Unsurprisingly, the Wildcats were at their best in the first set, which they won 25-23. They hit .457, scoring on 16 kills without an error. They returned to the court for the second set looking like a completely different team. West Virginia looked like a different team, too, but the Mountaineers went in a positive direction. WVU stayed steady in the number of kills while cleaning up its errors, acing Arizona three times, and getting three total blocks. The Mountaineers put together a 9-0 run that had them in front 16-5. It effectively ended the second set. Neither team could hold serve for long in the third set. Arizona’s biggest run was four points and West Virginia had a five-point run. The differences were the Mountaineers’ three-point run to start the set and the five straight points they won at the end. WVU went ahead early but Arizona took a lead at 15-14. From there, the two teams spent much of the third set simply trading points. The Wildcats went up by two at 18-16, but the Mountaineers tied it again at 19 points each. Arizona’s last lead came at 21-20. The team didn’t score another point in the set. WVU won the last five points to take a 2-1 lead in the match. Once again, a competitive set by Arizona was followed by a thoroughly uncompetitive set. The Wildcats only scored multiple points in a row three times in the set. Their biggest run was three points. WVU didn’t go on long runs, but it stayed steady. The Mountaineers would string together anywhere from two to four points at a time then quickly side out when Arizona won serve. Before long, the home team was up 16-10. The closest Arizona got was three points at 18-15, but WVU squashed the Wildcats’ hopes with a 4-0 run to pull within three points of the win. That run was part of a 7-2 advantage to close out the match. While the result wasn’t what Stubbs wanted, she didn’t feel it was for lack of competing. She was also pleased that her team didn’t have to go through a great deal of difficulty with travel this season. Two years ago, Arizona had to fly commercial for the road trip to Cincinnati and West Virginia. That included connecting flights and long bus rides. They had to bus between the two cities between matches and fly out of Pittsburgh after playing the Mountaineers. They returned home in the early morning hours of a Monday and players still had to attend classes. “It was a nightmare coming back because you got to be in Morgantown, you got to get to Pittsburgh, then you got to take a flight—then you got to take another flight,“ Stubbs said. This season, the team got to charter to Morgantown. After the game against the Mountaineers, they didn’t have to climb on a bus to head for Ohio. Instead, they got on another charter to fly to Cincinnati. They will fly commercial to Tucson after playing the Bearcats but that’s only because the first charter was not available until hours after the match in Cincinnati. The commercial flights would have them home sooner. “I thank the administration for it,” Stubbs said.

item.title: 🎙️ Mou, ahead of the Clásico: “Madrid win trophies with Mourinho”
item.description: 🎙️ Mou, ahead of the Clásico: “Madrid win trophies with Mourinho” José Mourinho played down the idea that the match against FC Barcelona would be a trial by fire ahead of El Clásico. “It isn’t. Madrid with Mourinho wins trophies,” the coach replied at a press conference. The Real Madrid coach said Barça’s defeat in Paris “tells me nothing” and that his mood would be the same if Madrid had lost 4-1 to Leipzig rather than won 4-1. He added that what happened in previous Clásicos and derbies “doesn’t mean much” and that Madrid are heading into the game in good shape and scoring goals. A Madrid side still taking shape Mourinho rejected the idea that his team is “a finished product” and described it as a project in its early stages. Excluding preseason and the international break, he said he had only had a month and a half of actual work with the players, who are still getting to know him, so comparing Madrid with a more established team “doesn’t seem fair to me”. "Far from being a finished product, it’s a product in its initial stages, where we’re at an early stage and the coach is getting to know it, analysing it...", the coach stressed. On the referee for El Clásico "The referee’s name never bothers me; I always start from the assumption that he’s good. What bothers me a little is when the rules are broken. So far, according to internal information, they haven’t been. Several referees’ names have come up. Nobody has told me, 'This is the referee.' Whoever it is, I hope it goes well for him," Mourinho reflected. On Lamine Yamal, the coach said that “they’re all very good” and that respecting the opposition is one thing, but “changing your plans or forgetting your identity” is another—something he will not do for him or anyone else. On the referee, he said he always assumes he is good and that, according to internal information, no rules have been broken. He also confirmed that he has decided on his starting eleven. Asked about comments from Fermín, who said he was tired of complaints about the Negreira case, Mourinho replied: “Maybe so. We’re tired of other things that keep happening.” El Clásico takes place tomorrow, a match that the coach described as “unique” because “the world stops to watch it”. item.title: Volkanovski vs Evloev: UFC 333 start time, undercard and how to watch fights
item.description: This weekend, Alexander Volkanovski and Petr Yan defend their titles in a major double-header at UFC 333 . In the main event in Abu Dhabi, Volkanovski puts his featherweight belt on the line against Movsar Evloev , who will bring an unbeaten record and tricky grappling style against the Australian icon. At 38 years old, the well-rounded Volkanovski will hope not to have lost a step , as the slightest drop-off could cost him against a fighter known for close decisions . Alexander Volkanovski during his second win over Diego Lopes (Getty) In the co-main event, Yan fights Merab Dvalishvili for the third time, having avenged a loss to the Georgian by outpointing him with a masterful showing in December. The bantamweight belt is up for grabs in that fight, just as it was in their second meeting, and a Yan victory could set up a great night for Russia if Evloev follows suit. When is UFC 333? UFC 333 will take place on Saturday 24 October at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. The early prelims will begin at 3pm BST (7am PT / 9am CT / 10am ET), followed by the regular prelims at 5pm BST (9am PT / 11am CT / 12pm ET), then the main card at 7pm BST (11am PT / 1pm CT / 2pm ET). How can I watch it? In the UK , the card will air live on TNT Sports and is also accessible via HBO Max, EE TV, Virgin Media, Amazon Prime Video, and Sky Sports. In the US , Paramount+ will stream the action. Odds Volkanovski – 10/11; Evloev – 10/11 Yan – 8/15; Dvalishvili – 6/4 Via Betway . Get all the latest UFC betting sites’ offers. item.title: 'I don't look back in anger' - Xabi Alonso opens up on 'premature' Real Madrid sacking as former Liverpool man reveals why he chose Chelsea move
item.description: Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso has reflected on his whirlwind tenure at Real Madrid, admitting that his dismissal from the Santiago Bernabeu dugout felt premature. The Spaniard, who arrived with a burgeoning reputation from Bayer Leverkusen, saw his stint in the Spanish capital cut short despite being active in multiple competitions. A premature end in the Spanish capital Los Blancos appointed Alonso at the start of last season following his impressive managerial breakthrough at Bayer Leverkusen. He enjoyed a bright start during the Club World Cup, but his reign ultimately unravelled midway through the campaign. Following a defeat in the Spanish Super Cup final in January, the Madrid hierarchy ruthlessly wielded the axe . The decision ended the Spaniard's project to overhaul the team's playing style before it had truly begun, with the club temporarily turning to Alvaro Arbeloa to steady the ship. 'I don't look back in anger' FBL-KSA-SUPERCUP-BARCELONA-REAL MADRID Speaking to former Liverpool team-mate Jamie Carragher on Sky Sports ’ programme Boss , Alonso expressed his frustration over the timing of his departure. However, the tactician insisted he holds no grudges against the Spanish giants. "I felt as though it finished a little bit earlier, before knowing if the season was going to end well," Alonso said. "It was the middle of the season. We were still in La Liga, the Champions League, but it was an experience to manage Real Madrid." He added: "Real Madrid is special in everything. It’s a little bit different to other clubs in everything. I learned from that, and I don’t look back in anger. I look back, thinking I tried and gave my best. Now I’m focusing on the future, but I had to try it." Embracing the Stamford Bridge project While Madrid ultimately pivoted to a vastly different approach by later appointing Jose Mourinho, Alonso quickly found a new home in west London. The Spaniard revealed that Stamford Bridge offered the perfect environment to rebuild following a necessary period of rest. "It was about the timing. For me it was the right timing after Bayer Leverkusen, after Real Madrid. I had my time off," Alonso told Carragher. "And I wanted to choose to have that good connection, that good feeling about where to go, and I know Chelsea. "I had no link [to the club], but what I heard… The potential is there, few things could change. And I thought that we could start this journey together. I feel [the squad] have a very strong base, the squad is very good. With some improvement, new signings of different profiles, we could have a solid team. "It was gonna be a project… We know it’s going to take some more years, but the first year is important and here we are, just starting. But so far the feeling is that we could be aligned, on the same page. That’s going to be important." item.title: Gasperini could deploy Pisilli behind Malen
item.description: Gasperini could deploy Pisilli behind Malen Gian Piero Gasperini’s Roma are preparing for the away match against Napoli with several lineup questions, particularly regarding the attacking options to partner Donyell Malen. The Dutch center forward will return after serving his suspension and will be the Giallorossi’s main attacking partner. Behind him, however, the coach will need to identify the best players to ensure quality and unpredictability, especially considering the absence of Paulo Dybala. Matias Soulé is ready to reclaim a starting spot, building on a strong start to the season marked by two goals and an assist in the first seven matchdays. Rodrigo Mora continues to be a key offensive option. The youngster, born in 2007, has shown promising qualities, but has yet to find the consistency needed to become a key player in the lineup. As reported by La Repubblica, Gasperini is evaluating various options for the attacking midfield, aiming to increase the team’s attacking threat. One of the possibilities concerns the advancement of Niccolò Pisilli behind Malen, a choice that will depend on Cristante’s condition and his possible presence from the first minute. Cristante’s possible return to the starting eleven could significantly alter the Giallorossi’s midfield structure. If the midfielder offers the necessary fitness, Gasperini could deploy him alongside De Roon in midfield, freeing up Pisilli for a more advanced role alongside Soulé. Otherwise, Mora’s chances of starting the game increase. In defense, however, the indications point to a resurgence of the trio of Mancini, Ndicka, and Hermoso, while Wesley is expected to occupy the left flank. On the right, Lulli appears favored over Molina, confirming the trust he has earned in recent months. Furthermore, the 2007-born player has reportedly already reached an agreement with the club for a contract renewal until 2031, with the signing expected on Monday. The trip to the Maradona stadium will also be an important opportunity to break a string of unfavorable precedents for Roma. The Giallorossi’s last victory away to Napoli dates back to March 3, 2018, when Eusebio Di Francesco’s team won 4-2. Their last away win against a team coached by Massimiliano Allegri was even further back in time, in 2010. Gasperini will try to reverse this trend, leveraging a standings position that currently sees Roma seven points ahead of the Azzurri. This is a significant advantage, but one that will need to be confirmed on the pitch.

item.title: Liverpool ready to wrap up £47m signing after recent performances
item.description: Liverpool ready to wrap up £47m signing after recent performances Ronald Araujo to Liverpool: Summer Decision Edges Closer Liverpool are gathering increasing encouragement in their assessment of Ronald Araujo, with the Uruguay international making an early impact that has strengthened the case for a permanent move next summer. According to Marca , the deal in place would require Liverpool to pay €55 million, around £47 million, if they choose to turn his stay into a full transfer. That figure remains significant, even for a club of Liverpool’s scale, and there is still time before any final call is made. Yet the direction of travel appears clear. Araujo’s adaptation has gone better than many anticipated, and his performances have opened a route towards the kind of regular role that had become harder to secure elsewhere. Ronald Araujo role under Andoni Iraola One of the more notable developments has been how Araujo has been used. Repositioned at full-back, he has delivered with authority in a role that demands tactical awareness, recovery speed and consistent concentration. His physical profile suits the position, while his defensive aggression has helped him compete effectively in wide areas. Added to that, he has offered a threat further forward, bringing a dimension Liverpool clearly value. There is a broader appeal here too. Araujo’s capacity to cover more than one role enhances his usefulness in a squad expected to compete across multiple fronts. That flexibility matters, especially for a head coach still shaping the group in his own image after taking charge at Anfield. Liverpool transfer stance on £47m option Iraola has publicly underlined that view. “Ronald needed this change and he has arrived with humility; he is an experienced player from a big club, prepared to play in different positions,” the Liverpool head coach said. It is a revealing endorsement, one that speaks both to the player’s mindset and to the staff’s belief that he can become a dependable part of the project. Araujo has also made his position clear, stressing that his immediate focus is on minutes, importance and rhythm rather than rushing any long-term discussion. “I think here I am finding what I needed, which was to play, feel important and show my football. It is very early to talk about these things. I am getting playing time, which is what I want and then we will see what happens in the future,” he said. Barcelona waiting on Araujo future That caution is understandable. Liverpool still need to decide whether €55 million, or roughly £47 million, represents the right value. Barcelona, for their part, are watching closely. The Spanish club would welcome that level of income in the next summer market, particularly if it allowed them to reinvest in greater experience for a youthful defensive unit. For now, the situation remains live rather than settled. Every appearance, every assured display and every contribution in both boxes adds weight to Araujo’s candidacy. The financial framework is already known. What follows on the pitch between now and next summer is likely to determine whether Ronald Araujo becomes a permanent Liverpool player. Our View This feels like one of those situations where the longer it goes on, the more obvious the answer becomes. If Araujo keeps performing like this, £47 million starts to look far more reasonable than risky. Elite defenders with top-level experience, physical authority and positional versatility do not come cheaply, and Liverpool have already seen enough to believe he can raise the floor and ceiling of the squad. item.title: Sky Sports: Arsenal ‘seriously interested’ in 22-year-old striker
item.description: Sky Sports: Arsenal ‘seriously interested’ in 22-year-old striker Arsenal Transfer Latest: Nicolo Tresoldi Interest Grows as Striker Plans Take Shape Arsenal’s striker planning is moving into sharper focus, with Sky Sports reporting that the club are “seriously interested” in Club Brugge forward Nicolo Tresoldi. The wider picture around Arsenal’s recruitment remains important here. Mikel Arteta wanted to add a central striker previously, but a move for Julian Alvarez did not get over the line. That has left the position under continued review, even if other attacking areas are also under consideration in longer-term planning. There is a clear conditional element to this developing situation. Arsenal’s next steps up front may depend heavily on Viktor Gyokeres and how his role evolves. Recent reporting has indicated uncertainty around his standing after slipping behind Kai Havertz in the pecking order, and that naturally has consequences for how aggressively Arsenal move in the market. Nicolo Tresoldi Profile Fits Emerging Arsenal Need Tresoldi’s numbers explain why Arsenal are paying attention. The 22-year-old has scored nine goals in 13 matches in all competitions this season and has also made a major impression in the Champions League, where he sits among the leading scorers. That follows a productive previous campaign in which he delivered 23 goals and nine assists. Arsenal already know plenty about the attacking environment around him at Club Brugge. Tresoldi operated alongside Christos Tzolis, who has since made his own move to north London. That familiarity may help Arsenal’s internal assessments, particularly when judging whether Tresoldi’s output can translate into a more demanding setting. Photo: IMAGO Arsenal Transfer Strategy Still Leaves Room for Alternatives Any move, if it advances, would likely be viewed through the lens of value as much as talent. A reported €20 million fee places Tresoldi in an interesting bracket, attractive enough to explore, but still significant for a player yet to prove himself in one of Europe’s top five leagues. That is the central question. Arsenal need more cutting edge and more reliability in front of goal, but they also need certainty. Tresoldi appears to offer sharp movement, penalty-box instincts and upward momentum, though signing him as a direct answer to a major attacking problem would carry risk. Alternative names remain in the background. Arsenal continue to be linked with Alvarez, while Bournemouth’s Eli Junior Kroupi is another player admired after an eye-catching rise. For now, Tresoldi belongs firmly in the conversation, and perhaps more seriously than before. Our View This feels like the kind of deal that could become very smart very quickly if Arsenal get the timing right. Tresoldi has the profile of a forward on the rise, and there is obvious appeal in moving before the price climbs beyond reach. That familiarity may help Arsenal’s internal assessments, particularly when judging whether Tresoldi’s output can translate into a more demanding setting. Photo: IMAGO Arsenal Transfer Strategy Still Leaves Room for Alternatives Any move, if it advances, would likely be viewed through the lens of value as much as talent. A reported €20 million fee places Tresoldi in an interesting bracket, attractive enough to explore, but still significant for a player yet to prove himself in one of Europe’s top five leagues. Tresoldi appears to offer sharp movement, penalty-box instincts and upward momentum, though signing him as a direct answer to a major attacking problem would carry risk. For now, Tresoldi belongs firmly in the conversation, and perhaps more seriously than before. Our View This feels like the kind of deal that could become very smart very quickly if Arsenal get the timing right. Tresoldi has the profile of a forward on the rise, and there is obvious appeal in moving before the price climbs beyond reach.
