A title-chasing side does not want to miss on a key striker signing, especially when margins at the top are so small. Even so, smart squads are built with a blend of certainties and emerging talent. Tresoldi looks like someone who could develop into a major asset under Arteta, particularly with creative players around him. If Arsenal see him as part of a broader attacking refresh rather than the only solution, this could be an excellent piece of business. The important thing now is clarity, decisiveness and making sure the next striker addition genuinely raises the level.

item.title: Dylan Harper Reacts to Spurs Starting Season With 0-2 Record
item.description: Dylan Harper Spurs Rockets Getty San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper shared his reaction to the team starting the season with a 0-2 record. After losing 116-104 in their season opener against the Oklahoma City Thunder, the Spurs lost on Friday night to the Houston Rockets 114-110 to drop to 0-2 this season. There is still a long season ahead for San Antonio, but fans are understandably frustrated by the team’s slow start after they went to the NBA Finals this past season. Harper, however, is not worried. Dylan Harper Not Worried About Spurs’ Slow Start Speaking to reporters following the Spurs’ loss to the Rockets on Friday night, Harper was asked to send a message to Spurs fans who are concerned about the team’s slow start, and this is what he said. “How many games are left? (80). Exactly. It’s not going to be perfect from Day 1. And if it was perfect and everything was beautiful and we played the right way, I would say there’s a problem. Obviously, we’re still figuring it out with the group we have, but I feel like, if you’re concerned this early, obviously you need to have that type of poise and that type of energy to get it right, but at the same time just having it in the back of your mind that you got a long way to go with this group,” Harper said. Spurs fans have concerns about the teams 0-2 start. I asked Dylan Harper what he’d say to those concerned, and his answer was this : 👀 @spurfectblog #PorVida pic.twitter.com/T1HboXpVBL — Carolina Teague (@CTtheMicSlayer) October 24, 2026 Big Game for Dylan Harper Although the Spurs lost, Harper had a big game for San Antonio as he scored 20 points on 8-of-15 shooting, while also adding 3 rebounds and 2 assists. After mostly coming off the bench in his rookie season last year, Harper has been moved to the team’s starting lineup by Spurs head coach Mitch Johnson this season. Although the Spurs are 0-2 so far this season, Harper has been playing well and is not to blame for the team’s two defeats. As Harper said, the season is long, and the Spurs still have 80 more regular-season games left to play this year. So, despite the team’s slow start, his message to the fans is clear: take a deep breath, and remember that it’s a long season. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Dylan Harper Reacts to Spurs Starting Season With 0-2 Record appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Lulli to pen new Roma deal on Monday
item.description: Lulli to pen new Roma deal on Monday Gian Piero Gasperini’s Roma team arrives at the Maradona stadium aiming to maintain their form and secure a significant result against Napoli. The Giallorossi coach, now among the select group of coaches to have achieved 300 Serie A victories, is preparing a team that will have to contend with some significant absences. Meanwhile, Roma have secured Lulli’s new contract. As confirmed by Gazzetta dello Sport , Lulli will sign a new deal until 2031. The player is expected to pen the new contract on Monday morning.

item.title: PSV vs Feyenoord: Match Preview, Team News and Predicted Lineups
item.description: PSV Eindhoven host Eredivisie leaders Feyenoord at the Philips Stadion on Sunday in the standout fixture of matchday 10, with Peter Bosz’s side looking to close the four-point gap at the top and revive their title defence. The first De Kraker of the season arrives at a crucial moment for both clubs. PSV have suffered two league defeats in their last three matches, while Feyenoord remain unbeaten in the Eredivisie and are aiming to extend their advantage over their closest challengers. Giovanni van Bronckhorst’s side have won five consecutive away league matches, but their recent record against PSV makes this a significant test. Feyenoord have lost their last five meetings with the Eindhoven club by an aggregate score of 14-4. PSV have to take the confidence from this victory into their next fixtures, starting with Feyenoord [IMAGO/Pro Shots] Match Preview PSV’s recent inconsistency has brought them back into the chasing pack after a five-match winning run propelled them to the top earlier in the campaign. Their latest setback came against ADO Den Haag , where Sven Mijnans opened the scoring before being sent off shortly before half-time. PSV subsequently surrendered their lead and suffered a dramatic 2-1 defeat when goalkeeper Matěj Kovář inadvertently turned the ball into his own net in stoppage time. That loss followed a 3-2 defeat against FC Twente , leaving Bosz’s men with work to do as they attempt to maintain their pursuit of a fourth consecutive Eredivisie title. However, PSV head into Sunday with renewed confidence after beating FC Porto 1-0 in the Champions League. Guus Til scored the decisive goal, and the victory offered a timely response following their domestic disappointments. Til’s goal ultimately proved to be the winner [IMAGO/Pro Shots] PSV have also remained unbeaten at home in the league, recording three wins and one draw. Their ability to impose themselves at the Philips Stadion could prove decisive against a Feyenoord side that has struggled badly in this fixture. Feyenoord, meanwhile, have won seven of their nine league matches and have not lost an Eredivisie game since March. Their domestic consistency has put them four points clear of PSV, although their five-match winning streak across all competitions ended recently. The Rotterdam club will also need to show greater defensive control after conceding three goals against Telstar. Despite that setback, they have recorded a league-high four clean sheets and possess several attacking threats capable of exploiting PSV’s defensive vulnerabilities. There is an added historical dimension to the contest. A year ago, Feyenoord arrived at this stage of the season unbeaten and ahead of PSV, only to lose 3-2 at the Philips Stadion. Van Bronckhorst’s players will be keen to avoid a similar outcome. PSV Receive Major Injury Boost Ahead of Feyenoord Clash as Five Players Return to Training Peter Bosz regains key reinforcements as the Eredivisie giants look to capitalize on European momentum and narrow the gap during Sunday’s high-stakes showdown against the league leaders. Team News PSV Eindhoven PSV will be without Mijnans , who is suspended following his red card against ADO Den Haag. Til is expected to move into the central attacking role, where his movement and five league goals could make him an important figure. Jerdy Schouten, Adamo Nagalo and Alassane Pléa remain unavailable. Kovář is expected to retain his place after his strong performance against Porto. Sergiño Dest, Lutsharel Geertruida , Yarek Gasiorowski and Filip Kostić are also in contention for defensive roles, although Armando Obispo could return to the starting lineup. Tjark Ernst should continue in goal behind a defence featuring Givairo Read, Jeremiah St. Juste, Mika Mármol and Javi López. Gjivai Zechiël, Charles Vanhoutte and Oussama Targhalline are expected to form the midfield, with Anis Hadj Moussa and Luciano Valente supporting striker Nacho Ferri. Ferri leads Feyenoord’s league scoring with six goals, while Hadj Moussa and Zechiël have five apiece. Read’s attacking contribution from right-back will also be important, having provided five assists and created seven big chances. Feyenoord: Ernst; Read, St. Juste, Mármol, López; Zechiël, Vanhoutte, Targhalline; Hadj Moussa, Ferri, Valente.

item.title: Serie A: Napoli vs. Roma – probable line-ups, where to watch on TV
item.description: Serie A: Napoli vs. Roma – probable line-ups, where to watch on TV Donyell Malen will lead the Roma attack in an away game at Napoli, but Paulo Dybala remains injured, and Massimiliano Allegri will look to Rasmus Hojlund. It kicks off at 18:00 CET [17:00 BST] at the Stadio Maradona. NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 10: Rasmus Hojlund of SSC Napoli is challenged by Giorgio Cittadini of Frosinone Calcio during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Frosinone Calcio at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 10, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) The home side must cope without Alisson Santos and David Neres, as well as Costantino Favasuli and Alessandro Buongiorno. Chelsea loanee Benoit Badiashile is the favourite over Amir Rrahmani at centre-back, as the latter is not fully fit and needs rest. Zambo Anguissa is favourite over Stanislav Lobotka in a midfield department completed by Kevin De Bruyne and Scott McTominay. ROME, ITALY – OCTOBER 20: Donyell Malen of AS Roma celebrates scoring his team’s fourth goal during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between AS Roma and SK Slovan Bratislava at Stadio Olimpico on October 20, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images) Roma, meanwhile, have travelled to Naples without Paulo Dybala, Manu Koné, Mile Svilar and Lorenzo Pellegrini. According to Sky Sport Italia, Dybala is close to returning to action as Roma hope the Argentine will be available for the upcoming mid-week round against Cagliari. There’s doubt over Nahuel Molina and Emanuele Lulli at right back, and over Rodrigo Mora and Bryan Cristante in the attacking midfield slot. Napoli vs. Roma – where to watch on TV The match will be broadcast live on TNT Sports 4, DAZN and HBO Max and on Paramount+ in the USA. Football Italia will provide live updates via a live blog. item.title: Real Madrid playmaker leads Europe in key creative statistic as Mourinho unlocks his potential
item.description: Real Madrid playmaker leads Europe in key creative statistic as Mourinho unlocks his potential Real Madrid midfielder Arda Guler is emerging as one of Europe’s most productive creative players after his positional transformation under Jose Mourinho. The Turkey international has performed exceedingly well since the start of the campaign, both as a right-winger and a deep-lying midfielder. According to Cadena SER , Guler averages 5.26 passes leading to a shot per game, the highest figure in Europe. His improvement under Mourinho is also reflected in his set-piece creativity and dribbling numbers. Guler’s attacking numbers improve significantly under Mourinho The 21-year-old has become an increasingly important creative force for Real Madrid through his passing ability and tendency to deliver dangerous balls into the penalty area. His set-piece statistics reveal a particularly striking improvement. Arda Guler has impressed under Jose Mourinho. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) Under former coach Xabi Alonso, Guler averaged 0.83 chances created from set pieces per game. That figure has increased to 2.54 under Mourinho, representing more than a threefold rise. His completed dribbles per game have also increased. The increase from 1.05 per game under Alonso to 1.75 under the Portuguese manager showcases Guler’s growing influence at Real Madrid . Rather than relying exclusively on his passing vision, he is increasingly capable of progressing possession himself and creating opportunities from dead-ball situations. Jose Mourinho is getting more from Real Madrid’s creative talent Guler’s development is particularly encouraging because Real Madrid have sometimes struggled to maintain consistent creativity in midfield. His technical ability gives Mourinho a player capable of unlocking compact defensive structures without depending entirely on individual brilliance from the forwards. Arda Guler has improved his delivery from corner situations. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) The improvement in set-piece production could also prove valuable in tightly contested matches, where a single accurate delivery can decide the outcome. With the likes of Dean Huijsen, Ibrahima Konate, Antonio Rudiger and Carlos Espi in the box, Real Madrid also have the aerial threats to convert from corner situations. With El Clasico approaching, his ability to control the game and create opportunities could be massive against Barcelona’s potent attacking structure. Real Madrid need players who can combine possession control with decisive actions in the final third, and Guler increasingly appears capable of providing both. It remains to be seen how the Turkey international fares for Real Madrid in the important game against Barcelona.

item.title: Roma to debut third kit vs Napoli
item.description: Roma to debut third kit vs Napoli Roma is preparing for their match against Napoli with a new kit. For today’s match at 6:00 PM at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, the Giallorossi will take to the field wearing their official third jersey for the first time this season. The kit has never been used in previous matches by Gian Piero Gasperini’s side. The away match against the Azzurri will therefore offer an opportunity to see a different version of the Roma kit in an important fixture in the Serie A calendar. Until now, Roma had only used the first two kits from their seasonal collection, alternating between the traditional red and the white one primarily used for away matches. The home kit has accompanied the Giallorossi in numerous matches, while the away version has served as a chromatic alternative when it was necessary to stand out from their opponents. The third kit, however, had remained unused in official matches, despite being part of the team’s existing kits. The Roma lineup is quite reshuffled for the big match against Napoli: Gollini will once again be in goal. The defense is expected to reassemble the Mancini-Ndicka-Hermoso trio. Lulli and Wesley are expected to operate on the wings, with the former competing against Molina. De Roon and Pisilli will be in midfield, with another play-off between Cristante and Mora in the attacking midfield, with the former slightly favored. Soulé and Malen complete the offensive line.

item.title: Red Bull identifies two "key focus" areas after Max Verstappen's promising start in Austin
item.description: Motorsport photo Max Verstappen finished Friday's practice sessions for the Formula 1 United States Grand Prix in second and third place. In both sessions, the four-time world champion was less than two tenths behind Charles Leclerc , who set the benchmark on both occasions. Red Bull is not immediately standing out from the rest of the field as it did in Malaysia, for example, but Verstappen is nevertheless largely satisfied with the early signs from the RB22 in Texas. Read Also: Max Verstappen slams “unacceptable” bumps at Austin F1 track: “It's out of control” "It's been a positive start to the weekend. This track is never easy when it comes to finding the right compromise between the low and high-speed corners", the Dutchman said after FP2. "The bumps make it even more difficult, so you’re trying to find a good balance in the car and get into a rhythm. That’s what we’ve been working on between FP1 and FP2. There’s still a bit more work to do to fine-tune that balance, but it wasn’t a bad day at all." In practical terms, this means teams have to find a compromise in two different ways this weekend. Given the varied layout of the Circuit of the Americas, the first concerns the balance between high-speed and low-speed corners. Based on the GPS data, Red Bull appears competitive in the high-speed sections, making technical director Pierre Wache very clear about what needs to improve. "It's clearly the low speed performance that we are focused on at the moment. Low speed is the key for us." That is reflected in the data. Comparing the fastest laps of Leclerc, Antonelli and Verstappen, the slowest corners on the circuit are predominantly coloured red – in other words, Ferrari territory. Leclerc is strong both on the brakes and on the exit of Turn 1, and shows the same pattern at Turn 11, the slow left-hander before the long straight. At the end of that long straight – just before the braking point – Verstappen is almost a tenth ahead of Leclerc's time, while Antonelli is more than two tenths ahead. However, Verstappen loses considerable ground through Turns 12 to 16, another slower section of the circuit. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing This underlines Wache's comments, although the challenge in Austin is not just about finding the right balance between different types of corners. Equally important is the compromise between outright performance and a car that can cope reasonably well with the bumps, which Verstappen described as "unacceptable" and "out of control" during Thursday's media day. "The car reacts to those bumps how you would expect, it's jumping a lot", Wache said when asked how the RB22 is dealing with the track conditions. "The track is massively bumpy, especially at Turn 1 under braking. You have to be very careful. But yeah, that’s the problem with this type of set-up that we are using. In both sessions, the four-time world champion was less than two tenths behind Charles Leclerc , who set the benchmark on both occasions. Red Bull is not immediately standing out from the rest of the field as it did in Malaysia, for example, but Verstappen is nevertheless largely satisfied with the early signs from the RB22 in Texas. Read Also: Max Verstappen slams “unacceptable” bumps at Austin F1 track: “It's out of control” "It's been a positive start to the weekend. This track is never easy when it comes to finding the right compromise between the low and high-speed corners", the Dutchman said after FP2. "The bumps make it even more difficult, so you’re trying to find a good balance in the car and get into a rhythm. That’s what we’ve been working on between FP1 and FP2. There’s still a bit more work to do to fine-tune that balance, but it wasn’t a bad day at all." In practical terms, this means teams have to find a compromise in two different ways this weekend. Given the varied layout of the Circuit of the Americas, the first concerns the balance between high-speed and low-speed corners. Based on the GPS data, Red Bull appears competitive in the high-speed sections, making technical director Pierre Wache very clear about what needs to improve. "It's clearly the low speed performance that we are focused on at the moment. Low speed is the key for us." That is reflected in the data. Comparing the fastest laps of Leclerc, Antonelli and Verstappen, the slowest corners on the circuit are predominantly coloured red – in other words, Ferrari territory. Leclerc is strong both on the brakes and on the exit of Turn 1, and shows the same pattern at Turn 11, the slow left-hander before the long straight. At the end of that long straight – just before the braking point – Verstappen is almost a tenth ahead of Leclerc's time, while Antonelli is more than two tenths ahead. However, Verstappen loses considerable ground through Turns 12 to 16, another slower section of the circuit. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing This underlines Wache's comments, although the challenge in Austin is not just about finding the right balance between different types of corners. Equally important is the compromise between outright performance and a car that can cope reasonably well with the bumps, which Verstappen described as "unacceptable" and "out of control" during Thursday's media day. "The car reacts to those bumps how you would expect, it's jumping a lot", Wache said when asked how the RB22 is dealing with the track conditions. "The track is massively bumpy, especially at Turn 1 under braking. You have to be very careful. But yeah, that’s the problem with this type of set-up that we are using. It is not as stiff as last year, but also not so far [away from that]. The car is not very compliant on the bumps here." By using the term set-up, Wache is not referring specifically to Red Bull's choices, but to the current generation of F1 cars. In theory, these should be slightly more comfortable over the bumps than the ground-effect cars of recent years, but Verstappen explained on Thursday that the opposite is actually the case. Thanks to active aerodynamics and straight mode, the cars rise slightly on the straights. This limits wear on the skid blocks and gives teams the freedom to push the limits even further in terms of ride height. As a result, the ride height is low under braking and through the corners, precisely the areas where the Circuit of the Americas is extremely bumpy. According to Wache, improving the car's behaviour over those bumps and its low-speed performance are Red Bull's two main priorities ahead of qualifying. item.title: Xabi Alonso welcomes “special” Chelsea–Tottenham Derby and urges Blues to keep cool
item.description: Xabi Alonso welcomes “special” Chelsea–Tottenham Derby and urges Blues to keep cool Xabi Alonso has said he is looking forward to the 'special' experience of a London Derby between Chelsea and Tottenham. Chelsea welcome their fierce rivals to Stamford Bridge in the Premier League this evening. Alonso's side are searching for a third consecutive Premier League win, and are aiming to continue a fine recent record in this fixture. Chelsea have won their last six meetings with Spurs in all competitions, and have lost just one league game against their London neighbours at Stamford Bridge in 34 meetings. Asked how he feels ahead of the game, Alonso expressed his excitement but warned Chelsea must keep their cool. Chelsea vs Tottenham: Alonso hails “special” London Derby and urges Blues to play with “heart and intelligence” "Every derby is special, you feel the energy and excitement from the stands. We need to use that energy on the pitch because we need to connect well," he said at his pre-match press conference. "We need to have good emotional control as well because there is a lot of passion and commitment from both sides. Playing football with heart is what we want." Despite Chelsea's recent dominance in the fixture, Alonso said past results count for little. He said the Blues must show 'heart' and 'intelligence' to take the points. "I knew about it [six-game winning run] but tomorrow is another game. We need to prove again that we can continue that run and knowing it is a special game so we need to play with heart, head and intelligence."

item.title: Man City Starting XI vs Aston Villa: Confirmed Team News and Predicted Lineup
item.description: Man City Starting XI vs Aston Villa: Confirmed Team News and Predicted Lineup Man City Team News vs Aston Villa: Erling Haaland Ready for Return Manchester City should have Erling Haaland back in the starting side for the trip to Aston Villa, and that is the headline. Enzo Maresca rotated in midweek, protected key players and now waits on three late fitness decisions before settling on his team for Villa Park. Haaland had been seen limping after the recent win over Ipswich, which raised the usual noise around his availability. Maresca has now shut that down. “Erling is the only one 100 per cent available,” he said, a clear indication that the striker is fit and ready to lead the line from the start. The uncertainty sits elsewhere. Nico O’Reilly, Matheus Nunes and Mateo Kovacic are all carrying knocks and all face checks ahead of kick-off. Maresca kept it simple: “We have a session this afternoon. They can be all available or not. Yesterday they were all improving, and we’ll see this afternoon.” That is not theatre. It is where things stand. Erling Haaland Boost for Man City Haaland changes the picture immediately. City can manage without a lot of players, few sides can casually replace a striker of his output. His return gives structure to the attack and clarity to everyone behind him. There is no need to overcomplicate it, if Haaland is fit, he starts. Behind him, Phil Foden made a strong case to keep his place after a midweek hat-trick. He looks the obvious option in the No 10 role, though Rayan Cherki is expected to come back into the side and offers Maresca another decision. If Cherki starts centrally, Foden can shift left. Iliman Ndiaye looks the likely option on the other flank. Photo IMAGO One forward option who will not feature is Antoine Semenyo. The knee injury he suffered against Ipswich is expected to keep him out for around eight weeks, which removes one of the more direct attacking alternatives from the squad. Enzo Maresca Awaits Midfield Verdict Midfield is less settled. Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez are expected to continue at the base, largely because the alternatives may not be ready. Kovacic and Nunes have both been dealing with knocks, and O’Reilly is in the same category. If none of the three make it, Maresca has fewer options for rotation and game management. That could also affect the full-back positions. Josko Gvardiol started in O’Reilly’s place in midweek and should continue on the left. Maresca appeared relaxed about the issue Gvardiol picked up late in that game, so there is little reason to expect a change there. On the right, Rayan Ait-Nouri may get a rare start if Nunes is not passed fit. It would not be a surprise. City have had to patch around injuries in recent weeks, and this is another case of availability dictating selection. Predicted Man City XI vs Aston Villa There is no mystery around the shape. item.title: Warriors' Yaxel Lendeborg defends verbal jousting with Luka Doncic: ‘He's not Michael Jordan'
item.description: Golden State Warriors forward Yaxel Lendeborg drives toward the basket as Memphis Grizzlies forward Cameron Boozer defends during the second quarter Friday at Chase Center. (Stephen Lam/S.F. Chronicle) This time Yaxel Lendeborg squared off against Cameron Boozer, not Luka Doncic. That made for a different type of duel, without any referendum on whether an NBA rookie should dare trade trash talk with one of the league's top players. Doncic's name still came up Friday night at Chase Center, and once again Lendeborg showed his penchant for biting honesty. "I'm always gonna be myself, man," Lendeborg said after he and the Golden State Warriors collapsed late and fell 111-108 to Memphis. "I don't care what anybody has to say about it. The guys on the couch talking bad about me, I couldn't care less. "I'm 24 and in the NBA, with the best job in the world. I just moved my mom out to California. I'm living a dream." So what feedback did Lendeborg hear after his verbal jousting with Doncic in the season opener 48 hours earlier? "I'm not supposed to talk to him, something like that," Lendeborg replied, chuckling. "C'mon now. He's gonna say what he wants to say and I'm gonna say what I want to say. I'm not afraid to talk to anybody. He's not Michael Jordan." Lendeborg acknowledged he "did take it overboard" during his postgame media session Wednesday night. That's when Lendeborg told reporters he "lost all respect" for Doncic, given his perpetual complaining to the officials in the Lakers' season-opening win over the Warriors in Los Angeles. Two nights later, in their home opener, Lendeborg and Golden State confronted fresh demons. The Warriors blew a 12-point lead in the final four minutes, absorbing a painful loss to Boozer and the Grizzlies. Lendeborg filled the stat sheet, scoring 18 points with 13 rebounds and six assists. He earned 12 free-throw attempts, a huge Warriors need with Jimmy Butler sidelined. Lendeborg also committed six turnovers, repeatedly dribbling into traffic and losing the ball. Boozer, the No. 3 overall pick in the June draft (eight spots ahead of Lendeborg), produced similar numbers - 25 points, 13 rebounds, six assists, six turnovers. Not visible on the stat sheet was the way Boozer drove right at Lendeborg and scored on him down the stretch, as Memphis mounted its stunning comeback. "I think I definitely threw the game away myself, because of all those turnovers," Lendeborg said. Warriors head coach Steve Kerr struggled to peer past those final few minutes, naturally, when the Grizzlies stitched together a 17-0 run to steal the win. But he found a slice of solace in the way his team's prized rookie became more assertive offensively, after a tentative first quarter. "Yaxel is going to get better and better," Kerr said. "He just has to get used to the NBA. I thought there were several plays where he kind of just launched himself into the defense, either trying to score or get fouled. Those are plays where he's going to learn to ma

Boozer, the No. 3 overall pick in the June draft (eight spots ahead of Lendeborg), produced similar numbers - 25 points, 13 rebounds, six assists, six turnovers. Not visible on the stat sheet was the way Boozer drove right at Lendeborg and scored on him down the stretch, as Memphis mounted its stunning comeback. "I think I definitely threw the game away myself, because of all those turnovers," Lendeborg said. Warriors head coach Steve Kerr struggled to peer past those final few minutes, naturally, when the Grizzlies stitched together a 17-0 run to steal the win. But he found a slice of solace in the way his team's prized rookie became more assertive offensively, after a tentative first quarter. "Yaxel is going to get better and better," Kerr said. "He just has to get used to the NBA. I thought there were several plays where he kind of just launched himself into the defense, either trying to score or get fouled. Those are plays where he's going to learn to make a jump stop and make the play behind him. "He's putting himself in some risky spots that he won't be doing a few weeks from now. … The game will slow down for him. He's going to be a great, great player." The dust-up with Doncic on Wednesday, while highly entertaining, did not change an inescapable reality for Lendeborg: The Warriors need him to make an immediate impact on the court. They begin this season wildly short-handed, and in danger of sliding into oblivion long before Butler and Moses Moody (potentially) return from their knee injuries in January or February. Kerr offered a fundamental request before Friday night's game, when he was asked about the basketball piece of Lendeborg's eventful debut against the Lakers - and what the Warriors need from him moving forward. "I need him to run the floor harder," Kerr said. "He has a tendency to coast a little in transition, so I want to see him run the floor harder. I think that will open up a lot of opportunities for him." Lendeborg ran hard down the court at times against Memphis, but Kerr is not wrong - Lendeborg often drifts at half-speed. He also came out curiously passive at first, perhaps spooked by the presence of 7-foot-3 Memphis center Zach Edey. Lendeborg did not attempt his first shot until more than three minutes into the second quarter. Later in the quarter, Edey twice blocked Lendeborg's shot on tentative drives to the basket. But Lendeborg also showed why he's quickly becoming a fan favorite, drawing louder applause in pregame introductions than anyone not named Stephen Curry or Draymond Green. On one play, Lendeborg spun around Jerami Grant to score on a twisting, left-handed layup. On another play, he baited Grant into a foul (Doncic-like) on the perimeter. Then he sealed Jaylen Wells on the low post, corralled a long pass from Green and dunked. "I didn't mind that stuff the other day," Kerr said of Lendeborg's exchanges with Doncic. "But as Steph said, you've got to back it up. That's the thing. We play the Lakers again next week (on Friday), so OK here you go. "So that was an interesting opening night, but for us as a staff it's really more about the small things that most people aren't going to be looking at, like help-side defense. He did a good job on Luka one-on-one (Wednesday), but we got torched by Luka as a team." Two nights later, the Warriors got torched by Boozer and Ty Jerome. Now comes another test, with the first back-to-back set of the young season. Al Horford (age/rest) and Brandin Podziemski (back soreness) are not expected to play Saturday night in Phoenix, and Curry and Draymond Green also could sit. So c'mon down, Yaxel, and take all the shots you want. "I would definitely have to be way more aggressive," Lendeborg, wearing a Chris Webber throwback Warriors jersey, said of likely facing the Suns without Curry. "I'm looking forward to it, to see how I do and how I step up to the challenge." Subscribe There’s more to San Francisco with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: Flavio Goncalves: Man United plan £42m January bid for Sporting Lisbon star
item.description: Flavio Goncalves: Man United plan £42m January bid for Sporting Lisbon star Manchester United are preparing to further invest in the attack in January after struggling to score goals this season. The Red Devils were keen to add a new left forward to their squad this summer, but failed to get a deal across the line. They have lived to regret that decision, with Marcus Rashford , Matheus Cunha and Patrick Dorgu all failing to impress in the role. The Dane, meanwhile, has dropped back to the left-back position, while Rashford’s future remains uncertain. United have scored just 15 goals in 11 games across all competitions, and now sit 13th in the Premier League table after seven games. They have also found the back of the net just four times in the last five games across all competitions, prompting talk of emergency attacking additions in the winter transfer window. It now appears that the English giants have found a target in the Primeira Liga. United want Flavio Goncalves According to Caught Offside , United and Chelsea both have their eyes on Sporting CP winger Flavio Goncalves. In his column for the website, journalist Mark Brus wrote: “Chelsea and Manchester United could both be readying January transfer window moves for the next big thing in Portuguese football, as first reported here by the Daily Briefing.” “The name on everyone’s lips at the moment is Sporting CP winger Flavio Goncalves, who has been scouted by a number of Premier League clubs while his current employers desperately look to tie him down to a new contract.” The 19-year-old rose through the ranks at Sporting CP before breaking into the senior side this season. Fast, two-footed and with an eye for goal, Goncalves has already scored three goals and registered one assist in nine games for the Portuguese club. The player is under contract until 2030, and the report states that he has a €60 million release clause in his deal. However, Sporting CP are keen to tie him down to a new deal with a higher release clause. United planning winter move Brus goes on to state that United are already planning a €45–50 million offer to test the waters in January, adding: “I’m reliably told by sources close to the agents industry that Chelsea and United are among the sides already preparing to test the waters with bids in the region of €45–50m for Goncalves this winter.” “Sporting are desperate not to sell, and will likely point to that €60m release clause, but it will be interesting to see if the player himself perhaps pushes for a move.” While the Portuguese club are keen to tie him down to a new deal, there has not been much progress regarding a renewal. Brus points out that Goncalves and his representatives could be waiting to assess offers in January before making a decision regarding a contract extension. One source told the journalist: “Chelsea and Man United have scouted Goncalves extensively and they’re now prepared to make offers directly to Sporting this January, that’s the current expectation.” “Sporting know they have a huge talent on their hands, but they hope to get him to agree to a new deal so they can sell him for more money later. There’s every expectation that he could be a €100m player, so they won’t want to lose him on the cheap earlier than they need to.” Final Thoughts Goncalves could be an exciting addition to United’s attack, but his lack of top-flight experience could add a degree of risk to the move. The Red Devils, as such, should also target a proven name alongside the Portuguese winger in January. Why? ✅ United could be tempted to strengthen their attack in January. ⚠️ Caught Offside is not considered a particularly reliable source for United transfer news. TPP view We believe Goncalves could be on United’s radar, but reports that the club are preparing a January move for the Sporting Lisbon winger may be premature.

item.title: Juventus injury crisis deepens with two more players sidelined
item.description: Juventus injury crisis deepens with two more players sidelined Injuries have continued to disrupt Juventus at a difficult point in their season, with the Bianconeri confirming two fresh setbacks as they struggle to find consistent form. The latest developments will be a concern for Luciano Spalletti, whose position at the club is already under scrutiny as he attempts to stabilise the team and improve results. The Juventus manager needs his key players to remain fit and perform consistently if the club are to overcome their current difficulties. However, recurring injury problems have made it harder for him to establish stability, forcing him to contend with further disruption to his plans. Spalletti will be disappointed to lose more players at such an important stage of the campaign, particularly when Juventus need to build momentum and deliver better performances. The latest injuries could leave the manager with additional selection problems as he prepares for the team’s upcoming fixtures. Juventus confirm two fresh injury setbacks According to Football Italia , Juventus have confirmed that Nicolas Gonzalez and Zeki Celik have suffered fresh injuries following their involvement in the match against Rennes. The news represents another setback for the Bianconeri, who are already working to improve their performances and results. Celik’s injury will be particularly frustrating given his contribution against Rennes. The Turkiye international scored Juventus’ opening goal in the 2-2 draw , providing an important attacking contribution before the latest development threatened to interrupt his progress. His absence could leave Spalletti with another problem to address as he considers his options for the matches ahead. Juventus will need to assess the extent of the injury and determine how long the defender is likely to remain unavailable. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Gonzalez faces a spell on the sidelines Gonzalez is also set to miss time through injury, dealing Juventus another blow as they attempt to improve their form. The player recently signed a new contract at the club , reflecting the confidence placed in him following his resurgence this season. Juventus had hoped he would continue building on that progress and make an important contribution to their campaign. His injury therefore comes at an unwelcome moment, particularly with the team needing reliable performances from its key players. The club will hope to help both players recover as quickly as possible, although Gonzalez is expected to miss several weeks and could be unavailable for multiple matches. His absence will leave Spalletti with fewer options as he looks to guide Juventus through a challenging period.

item.title: “He will get his chance”: Arteta insists Gyokeres still has a role to play at Arsenal
item.description: “He will get his chance”: Arteta insists Gyokeres still has a role to play at Arsenal Mikel Arteta has insisted that he 'loves' Viktor Gyokeres and has said the out-of-favour Arsenal forward will get his chance this season. Gyokeres has struggled for minutes this season and is yet to start a game in the Premier League. The Swedish striker has played only 80 minutes of league football across four substitute appearances. Gyokeres was Arsenal's leading scorer last season with 21 goals in 55 appearances, and has been linked with an exit amid his lack of football. The 28-year-old came off the bench and provided an assist during Arsenal's 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League in midweek, and Arteta has insisted that Gyokeres has a role to play this season. Speaking at his pre-game press conference ahead of today's clash with Everton, Arteta declared his affection for both Kai Havertz and Gyokeres as centre-forward options. Arsenal go into the game in strong form, having won 11 of their first 13 competitive matches this season, including six out of seven in the Premier League . Arteta backs out-of-favour Gyokeres: “I love him” as Arsenal striker waits for his chance Asked about his options in attack, Arteta spoke warmly about both players and the bond he shares with them. "I love Kai Havertz, I love Viktor Gyökeres a lot. He has a very different character to Kai, but he's someone that you really feel close to. He's a very important player for the team, and he will have his chance." Arteta also addressed David Raya's recent comments, after the Spain goalkeeper said he would like to play in La Liga at some point in his career. The Arsenal boss joked that Raya "has to play in Spain at some point... on the beach with his friends, in the summer", before adding: "But for the next few years, he needs to play here for Arsenal!"

item.title: The three Newcastle United transfers that have made this season a struggle
item.description: Johan Manzambi Goal Aston Villa v Newcastle United Premier League It has not been a great start to the Newcastle United season. On the one hand, United have navigated two rounds of the Carabao Cup and are currently still only five points off 4th despite languishing in 11th. On the other hand, Newcastle have lost three of their last four games, appear to be unable to score, devoid of ideas and creativity, have a midfield that doesn’t function and is constantly walked through and are only four points off our friendly neighbours at the very bottom of the table. It’s still early days with only seven Premier League games played. I’m going to go all Steve McClaren here and say I’ll judge Jaissle after 10 games. He’s only just come into the job, he’s had a bundle of injuries and is working with a load of new, mainly inexperienced signings. Our next three league games are Crystal Palace away, Everton at home and Fulham away. Win a couple of those and we’ll be looking up the table again. Get a point or less, there’s every chance we’re in the relegation zone at the end of that sequence. If Everton dump us out of the Carabao Cup, with our game at the Hill Dickinson sandwiched in this run, morale of the fans and the squad will be incredibly low. The next run of fixtures after that are Arsenal at home, Brighton away, Man Utd at home and Sunderland at home. That is not a run of Premier League fixtures you want to be heading into whilst sat in the bottom three. Matty Jaissle's Black And White Army Banner Newcastle United Photo by The Mag What’s gone wrong? Well loads, clearly. But for me, there are three Newcastle United transfers that have hugely impacted our potential this season. Two agreed deals that changed their minds and one that should’ve never been allowed to happen. Victor Munoz – deal agreed, fanbase excited. Allegedly, we’d been negotiating a price under his buy out clause. We managed to agree a fee and then Liverpool came in, paid the clause and wrapped up the deal within no time. We quickly pivoted and snapped up Bazoumana Toure instead. From what I have seen of both players, Liverpool got a considerably better deal. In the here and now at least. It’s early days and Toure is three years younger than the lad we missed out on. But he’s lightweight and seems erratic. Whilst he has grabbed a couple of goals, I haven’t been impressed with his overall performances so far whereas what I’ve seen of Munoz, he looks a proper player. Quick, strong and technically able. He would have comfortably been a regular starter for us had we managed to seal his signing. On the one hand, United have navigated two rounds of the Carabao Cup and are currently still only five points off 4th despite languishing in 11th. On the other hand, Newcastle have lost three of their last four games, appear to be unable to score, devoid of ideas and creativity, have a midfield that doesn’t function and is constantly walked through and are only four points off our friendly neighbours at the very bottom of the table. It’s still early days with only seven Premier League games played. I’m going to go all Steve McClaren here and say I’ll judge Jaissle after 10 games. He’s only just come into the job, he’s had a bundle of injuries and is working with a load of new, mainly inexperienced signings. Our next three league games are Crystal Palace away, Everton at home and Fulham away. Win a couple of those and we’ll be looking up the table again. Get a point or less, there’s every chance we’re in the relegation zone at the end of that sequence. If Everton dump us out of the Carabao Cup, with our game at the Hill Dickinson sandwiched in this run, morale of the fans and the squad will be incredibly low. The next run of fixtures after that are Arsenal at home, Brighton away, Man Utd at home and Sunderland at home. That is not a run of Premier League fixtures you want to be heading into whilst sat in the bottom three. Matty Jaissle's Black And White Army Banner Newcastle United Photo by The Mag What’s gone wrong? Well loads, clearly. But for me, there are three Newcastle United transfers that have hugely impacted our potential this season. Two agreed deals that changed their minds and one that should’ve never been allowed to happen. Victor Munoz – deal agreed, fanbase excited. Allegedly, we’d been negotiating a price under his buy out clause. We managed to agree a fee and then Liverpool came in, paid the clause and wrapped up the deal within no time. We quickly pivoted and snapped up Bazoumana Toure instead. From what I have seen of both players, Liverpool got a considerably better deal. In the here and now at least. It’s early days and Toure is three years younger than the lad we missed out on. But he’s lightweight and seems erratic. Whilst he has grabbed a couple of goals, I haven’t been impressed with his overall performances so far whereas what I’ve seen of Munoz, he looks a proper player. Quick, strong and technically able. He would have comfortably been a regular starter for us had we managed to seal his signing. Of course, it was him that earned the penalty against us, so we may have won that opener against Liverpool had he not been amongst their ranks. Johan Manzambi – another one where we’d agreed everything. Manzambi asked for some time before signing the deal. That time, it appears, was spent speaking to Aston Villa who quickly unveiled him as their new acquisition. The Athletic have speculated that Manzambi was the club’s and Howe’s top target and that losing out on him was the final straw that saw Eddie Howe decide he couldn’t continue. Manzambi is quickly looking like one of the signings of the season. He can play anywhere across the midfield and has the skill and energy to dominate a game, as he did for large periods against us. When we lost out on him, we instead signed Aladji Bamba who has since only been trusted with 27 minutes of football. With teams regularly moseying through our midfield, you have to wonder how the powerful stopper we signed isn’t getting a look in. Manzambi predictably popped up with the winner in our most recent fixture. That’s two of our near signings playing a significant part in taking points from us. Team Huddle Newcastle United v Aston Villa St James' Park Premier League Photo by The Mag Bruno Guimaraes – this is the transfer that should have never been allowed to happen. I understand that he wanted to leave. The board allegedly said they would have resisted all efforts from Arsenal (or anybody else) to sign him had he been committed to staying. It was also made a bit easier for everyone with a new manager coming in as the blame wouldn’t be attached to Matthias Jaissle for Bruno departing. I personally think that Bruno expressing his desire to leave was the moment that sealed Howe’s decision. How could Howe be expected to rebuild the team without his talisman? He’d lost Gordon, Tonali and Trippier already. A huge overhaul was required but it would be a whole lot harder with the absence of a man that we rarely won a game without during Howe’s tenure. I wrote an article at the start of the summer, long before Bruno’s head was turned, asking if we could afford to lose him for nothing. My argument in that piece was that I’d rather have Bruno Guimaraes for the remaining years of his contract and see him leave for nothing, than accept £80m for him in the summer. The rationale was simple. Bruno was everything to us. He set the tempo, he led with passion, he had the ability to retain possession and find a killer pass. He had game winning interventions. A match that really stands out in my mind was one against Fulham last season. We were 1-1 and Bruno was single handedly trying to drag us to the three points. He missed a couple of good opportunities, you could see the rage and frustration emanating from him. And then Osula came on, broke away and forced the keeper into a save. Bruno came surging onto the loose ball and slotted it home to win the game and all that emotion roared free of him. I could see how much joy it gave him to earn that win for his team. Seeing him netting winning goals for Arsenal is so hard. Watching him kiss that badge and cupping his ears just doesn’t look right. He should still be at this club, wearing the armband and pulling this team together. Bruno said that he wanted to move to Arsenal but wouldn’t do anything to tarnish his standing with Newcastle fans. I think we should have tested that. In truth, he’s already tarnished his reputation with many just by leaving. For me, I believe he deserves our respect and appreciation. He gave us four and half wonderful years, led us to our first trophy in generations and truly lived and breathed Newcastle United in his time here. He’ll never feel that same level of love at Arsenal and for all the trophies he may win, I think he’s sacrificed something a lot more special. Mike Ashley is a bloke I will despise for the rest of my days. I still refuse to shop in Sports Direct. He sold all our best players again and again but he always did it on his terms. When Arsenal came calling for Cabaye, and our French midfielder went on a brief strike, Ashley didn’t sell as the Gunners hadn’t met his asking price. I’d like to see a little bit of that from our current management. If Bruno didn’t want to tarnish his reputation, I think the board should have appreciated how important he’s been to us in recent seasons and told him we’ve let too many key players go and he had to stay. He could have been offered a pay rise with a couple of years extension on his contract and if he’d turned that down the board should have just said, fine but you’re staying this season and then we’ll assess this situation next year. Sure, his value may have halved but would you rather have Bruno leading the team out or a spare £35 million or so to chuck at another untested player who may or may not be a success? At that point Bruno may have acted out and then he would have tarnished his reputation with most of us and rightly so. Or he hopefully would have knuckled down and helped this team. We’ve set such a dangerous precedent now. We’re getting decent transfer fees for our players but we’re falling into a habit of saying players can leave the moment they suggest they’d like to. item.title: Jackson Chourio Reacts After Brewers Beat Rays 3-2 in Game 1
item.description: Jackson Chourio Brewers Braves Getty Milwaukee Brewers left fielder Jackson Chourio shared his reaction to the Brewers’ 3-2 win against the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 1. The Brewers took a 2-0 lead in the first inning and never looked back, as they edged out a competitive 3-2 win in a game that went down to the final pitch. Chourio led off the game for the Brewers with a single, scoring on a Christian Yelich triple, and then added an RBI single in the seventh inning, scoring shortstop Cooper Pratt, to help Milwaukee take a 1-0 series lead in the 2026 World Series. Jackson Chourio Reacts to Big Game 1 Win Speaking to Sportsnet’s Hazel Mae after the Brewers won Game 1, Chourio shared his reaction to Milwaukee’s big win. “I’m just super happy. This moment, the fans, the support. I’m trying to enjoy it as much as I can,” Chourio said. "I'm just super happy. This moment, the fans, the support. I'm trying to enjoy it as much as I can." Jackson Chourio spoke with @thehazelmae moments after he helped the Brewers take a 1-0 lead in the 2026 #WorldSeries pic.twitter.com/3nuG9H9XwQ — Sportsnet (@Sportsnet) October 24, 2026 Brewers Favored to Win the World Series The Brewers were favored to win the World Series heading into it , and nothing changed after an important Game 1 victory over a scrappy Tampa Bay squad. Milwaukee has never won a World Series in the franchise’s entire history, but they have a great chance to do so this season, as the team is now just three wins away from capturing the championship. Chourio is one of Milwaukee’s best players , and he showed in Game 1 why the team has so much faith in him as their leadoff hitter. His single to open the game led to him coming in to score a run when Brewers team captain Yelich knocked him in, and then he had a big RBI single later in the game that ultimately proved to be the game-deciding run. This Brewers team is a ton of fun to watch as they have a great three-pronged attack of elite pitching, a potent lineup, and excellent defense on the field, making them a very difficult opponent for any team to handle in the league. That being said, the Rays are also dangerous, and although Milwaukee drew first blood in Game 1, don’t be surprised if this series needs the full seven games to decide a winner. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Jackson Chourio Reacts After Brewers Beat Rays 3-2 in Game 1 appeared first on HEAVY .
item.content:encoded: Jackson Chourio Brewers Braves Getty Milwaukee Brewers left fielder Jackson Chourio shared his reaction to the Brewers’ 3-2 win against the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 1. The Brewers took a 2-0 lead in the first inning and never looked back, as they edged out a competitive 3-2 win in a game that went down to the final pitch. Chourio led off the game for the Brewers with a single, scoring on a Christian Yelich triple, and then added an RBI single in the seventh inning, scoring shortstop Cooper Pratt, to help Milwaukee take a 1-0 series lead in the 2026 World Series. Jackson Chourio Reacts to Big Game 1 Win Speaking to Sportsnet’s Hazel Mae after the Brewers won Game 1, Chourio shared his reaction to Milwaukee’s big win. “I’m just super happy. This moment, the fans, the support. I’m trying to enjoy it as much as I can,” Chourio said. "I'm just super happy. This moment, the fans, the support. I'm trying to enjoy it as much as I can." Jackson Chourio spoke with @thehazelmae moments after he helped the Brewers take a 1-0 lead in the 2026 #WorldSeries pic.twitter.com/3nuG9H9XwQ — Sportsnet (@Sportsnet) October 24, 2026 Brewers Favored to Win the World Series The Brewers were favored to win the World Series heading into it , and nothing changed after an important Game 1 victory over a scrappy Tampa Bay squad. Milwaukee has never won a World Series in the franchise’s entire history, but they have a great chance to do so this season, as the team is now just three wins away from capturing the championship. Chourio is one of Milwaukee’s best players , and he showed in Game 1 why the team has so much faith in him as their leadoff hitter. His single to open the game led to him coming in to score a run when Brewers team captain Yelich knocked him in, and then he had a big RBI single later in the game that ultimately proved to be the game-deciding run. This Brewers team is a ton of fun to watch as they have a great three-pronged attack of elite pitching, a potent lineup, and excellent defense on the field, making them a very difficult opponent for any team to handle in the league. That being said, the Rays are also dangerous, and although Milwaukee drew first blood in Game 1, don’t be surprised if this series needs the full seven games to decide a winner. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Jackson Chourio Reacts After Brewers Beat Rays 3-2 in Game 1 appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Older, calmer, but still playing the hits: Mourinho and Madrid primed for clásico
item.description: Once Bobby Robson’s translator at the Camp Nou, Mourinho is tasked with bringing down Barcelona on Sunday José Mourinho has done the por que?, the printout and the press conference no-show, and he’s been here only three months. The Real Madrid manager has played the classics without even playing a clásico. Not yet anyway, but it’s time: on Sunday night he returns to the stadium he first arrived at 30 transformative years ago as Bobby Robson’s talented young translator, and last visited in 2013 as the most famous manager in football. The coach who once declared “today, tomorrow and always, Barcelona in my heart,” and claimed he would only ever go to Real Madrid to destroy them, has been entrusted with attempting to bring about the destruction of Barcelona. It is not the first time: if his return is about nostalgia, which it is, that’s wrapped up in their rivals too. Continue reading...

item.title: Arteta concerned over Saka’s durability as forward faces possible six-week absence
item.description: Arteta: ‘We need to understand how to manage his load’ Max Dowman could play against Everton on Saturday Mikel Arteta has expressed concern over Bukayo Saka’s robustness after a series of injuries to the forward in the past year and as he awaits further news on how long he will be out for with a thigh issue. Saka is set for an MRI scan after limping off in the 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League, with Arteta revealing the 25-year-old had “quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury”. Saka will definitely miss Saturday’s game against Evertonand, it is understood, Arsenal fear it could be a grade-two tear that could potentially keep him out for up to six weeks. Continue reading...

item.title: Enciso rescues point in storm for Ipswich to deny Nottingham Forest
item.description: Amid a Suffolk squall, winds whipping, a constant drum of rain, an encounter full of half-chances, mistakes, the obligatory refereeing controversy and searching questions. Do Ipswich possess the stones to deal with the big league? Perhaps so. How long can Nottingham Forest’s dip sustain before their president, Evangelos Marinakis, takes his usual course of action. Perhaps not much longer. Ipswich’s Gary O’Neil was the happier manager, Forest had created the cleaner opportunities, only for familiar failings to cost them. “We were never quite good enough with the ball to turn it into a football match,” said O’Neil. Further adding to Forest’s disappointment, Ipswich’s Issa Diop escaped what looked, on first glance, a red card for a last-man foul. A first-half exchange of goals, both owing much to defensive laxness, determined the result. Continue reading...

item.title: NWSL drops controversial criteria around ‘Rodman Rule’ in settlement with NWSLPA
item.description: Any player will be eligible for High Impact Player status Requirements had included top 100, marketability lists Sides also resolve grievance on Rodman contract refusal The NWSL and the NWSL Players Association have reached a settlement to drop the restrictive criteria around the controversial High Impact Player (HIP) rule, allowing any player to earn the league’s highest salaries. The NWSL introduced the rule late last year, allowing teams to spend an additional $1m above the salary cap to sign star players. Players with the designation had to meet one of eight criteria, ranging from US national team minutes and Ballon d’Or recognition to NWSL Best XI honors to media lists, including the Guardian’s Top 100 and a ranking that ordered athletes by marketability. Continue reading...

item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Mamdani loves Arsenal. He should challenge them to cut ties with the UAE over Sudan | Sasha Lezhnev and John Prendergast
item.description: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. But today, two of his biggest passions are on a collision course. On one hand, Mamdani is now arguably the US’s most high-profile supporter of English Premier League champions Arsenal. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. He wrote an essay about what Arsenal’s championship means to him, talks about Arsenal at press conferences and interviews and inaugurated Thierry Henry Way near Times Square in honor of the Arsenal legend. Continue reading...

item.title: Crystal Palace and Newcastle face off with both in search of season kickstart
item.description: Pierre Sage and Matthias Jaissle face some key questions: both were appointed this summer yet form, and results, have proved elusive Conceding 17 goals in seven Premier League matches is not exactly the start Pierre Sage or Crystal Palace’s hierarchy would have hoped for. The transition from Oliver Glasner’s counterattacking 3-4-2-1 formation to the Frenchman’s more aggressive approach has exposed massive weaknesses in defence, culminating with last week’s humiliating defeat at Brighton. Palace fans became used to success under Glasner and they are already looking nervously over their shoulders at the bottom three. Even their league wins under Sage so far – against Fulham and Nottingham Forest – could have ended in defeat. Something doesn’t seem right in south London. EA Continue reading...

item.title: Slegers and misfiring Arsenal badly need a result in WSL north London derby
item.description: Gunners’ title hopes have seemingly evaporated and their under-pressure head coach faces her latest test against Spurs on Saturday It says much about Arsenal’s predicament that the team who have conceded 12 goals in two games are not the side whose head coach is under most pressure before a north London derby. Tottenham, four points above their neighbours before Saturday’s meeting, may have been humbled in consecutive Women’s Super League matches but all eyes are on Renée Slegers. Arsenal are winless in five WSL matches for the first time, and the most decorated club in English women’s football desperately need a turning point. Their failure to beat Birmingham at home last Saturday, dropping points against a promoted side for the second time this season, again demonstrated the team’s inability to convert possession into goals. They increasingly look like a team stuck in Groundhog Day. Continue reading...

item.title: Pascal Gross: the obsessive runner keeping Brighton ‘one step ahead’ after fast start
item.description: Midfielder ‘who can never stand still’ has brought renewed energy to Seagulls since return to the club in January Most footballers like to spend their summers unwinding after a long season but not Pascal Gross. Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 , the midfielder entered – and won – a running race. Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. He is not known as someone who courts attention, and his victory by more than a minute came to light only when a video was posted on social media by a competitor. Continue reading...

item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...

item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

item.description: Funds for 2027 will match men’s World Cup in 2026 Players given better flights and individual hotel rooms Teams in the 2027’s Women’s World Cup in Brazil will receive the same preparation money from Fifa as those that played at the 2026 men’s tournament, the world’s governing body has announced. The preparation money for the 32 teams has been more than doubled to $2.5m (£1.86m) each. In 2023, the total preparation money for the tournament was $31m; it will now be $80m. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Does anyone feature on more than two clubs' all-time top-10 scoring charts? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the longest kit supply partnerships, more own goals (part II) and consecutive goalless draws Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Harry Kane is now Bayern’s seventh-highest scorer of all time, as well as being Tottenham’s highest scorer. The man he overtook at the top of that list, Jimmy Greaves, is also Chelsea’s seventh-highest scorer of all time. Do any other players feature on two (or more) clubs’ all-time top- 10 scoring charts?” asks Owen Powell. A trawl through the Knowledge archive reminded us that we have previously looked at players who are the record goalscorer for more than one club . This question is slightly different, as we’re focusing on goalscorers who are in the all-time top 10 for the most different clubs. There are dozens of players who appear for two clubs, including Sergio Ag üero (Atlético Madrid and Manchester City), Kenny Dalglish (Celtic and Liverpool), Jimmy Greaves (Chelsea and Tottenham) , Lionel Messi (Barcelona and Inter Miami), Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid and Al-Nassr) and Alan Shearer (Blackburn and Newcastle). Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...
